definition_en: a statement or sign that someone intends to harm you, or a person or thing likely to cause danger
core_image: 有人把拳头举在半空，还没落下，空气先紧了一层
scene: 山脚的村子连下了半个月的雨,老人盯着裂开的山脊不肯睡。 The cracked hillside was a threat to every house in the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 threat 是「威胁、危险的事物」（第 3 个义项：可能造成危害的人或事物）；句意为裂开的山坡对山谷里每座房子都是威胁。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「威胁；恐吓；危及」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「威胁的；凶险的」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受到威胁的；濒危的」

senses.title: A stated intention to harm
senses.definition: a warning, spoken or written, that someone will hurt or punish you if you do not do something
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面警告，若不照做就会受到伤害或惩罚
senses.example: He made a threat that he would report the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 他威胁说要举报那笔失踪的钱。
senses.why: The root means to press or squeeze: a threat is pressure applied before any blow falls.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「压、挤」：威胁是在拳头落下之前施加的压力。

senses.title: The feeling of danger
senses.definition: a sense that harm is close, whether or not words have been spoken
senses.definitionCN: 感到伤害临近，无论是否有人说过什么
senses.example: The quiet in the room carried a threat that none of them could name.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里那片安静带着一种谁也说不清的威胁。
senses.why: The noun can name a felt pressure even when nobody has spoken a word.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有人开口，这个名词也能命名一种被感觉到的压迫。

senses.title: A person or thing that endangers
senses.definition: a person, group or thing likely to cause harm or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害或麻烦的人、群体或事物
senses.example: Rising sea levels are a threat to low-lying islands.
senses.exampleCN: 海平面上升对低洼岛屿是一种威胁。
senses.why: Pressure can come from a storm as easily as from a person, so the word names the source too.
senses.whyCN: 压力可以来自一场风暴，也可以来自一个人，于是这个词也用来命名那个源头。

senses.title: A sign of coming harm
senses.definition: an early sign that something bad is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事可能发生坏结果的早期迹象
senses.example: Those dark clouds were a threat of hail.
senses.exampleCN: 那些乌云是冰雹的凶兆。
senses.why: A threat can be read in the sky before it is ever spoken: the sign itself carries the pressure.
senses.whyCN: 威胁可以在开口之前就读到天上：兆头本身就带着那股压力。

intro.en: Threat is a native English word from a Germanic root meaning to press or squeeze, the same pressure image behind throng.
intro.cn: threat 是英语本土词，源自意为「压、挤」的日耳曼词根，throng「拥挤」背后是同样的压迫意象。

items.en: The root carried the idea of pressing, crowding or forcing, a physical pressure on someone.
items.cn: 这个词根带有「压、挤、逼迫」之意，是对某人施加的实体压迫。

items.en: Old English þreat meant a crowd or a troop as well as pressure and compulsion, an army being pressure in human form.
items.cn: 古英语 þreat 既指人群、队伍，也指压迫与强制，一支军队就是人形的压力。

items.en: Middle English narrowed the word to the danger a hostile force represents, whether words or warriors.
items.cn: 中古英语把词义收窄为敌对力量所代表的危险，无论那是言语还是兵马。

items.en: The verb threat was replaced by threaten, built with the -en ending, and the noun kept the plain form.
items.cn: 动词形式 threat 被以 -en 结尾的 threaten 取代，名词则保留原形。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to impersonal dangers, so a virus or a rising sea can be a threat.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词扩展到非人的危险，病毒或上涨的海面都能成为威胁。

note.en: The first group gathers the threat family and near spellings; the second compares words for warnings and danger.
note.cn: 第一组收 threat 词族与形近词；第二组比较表示警告与危险的词。

entries.definition: The verb, to say or show that you will harm someone.
The adjective for behaviour or weather that menaces.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「威胁的、凶险的」

entries.definition: A thin line of fibre; one letter apart but from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 线；与 threat 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: To behave towards someone or give medical care; the spelling is close, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 对待；治疗（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: A statement that something bad may happen; it informs rather than pressures.
entries.definitionCN: 警告（重在告知，而非施压）

entries.definition: A serious threat or a threatening person; stronger in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；危险人物（语气更强）

entries.definition: The general possibility of harm, without anyone intending it.
entries.definitionCN: 危险（泛指伤害的可能，无人有意）

entries.definition: The act of frightening someone into doing what you want, often by law.
entries.definitionCN: 恐吓（常指以恐吓迫使服从，法律用词）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the pressing root, the verb family, and the wide modern use.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「压」的词根、动词词族，以及现代扩展的用法。

normal.en: The root means to press, and a threat is pressure put on before anything is done.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压」，威胁是在事情发生前施加的压力。

normal.en: Threaten is the verb, built with -en, and the noun stays short.
normal.cn: threaten 是加 -en 构成的动词，名词则保持短小。

normal.en: An empty threat has no army behind it, only words.
normal.cn: empty threat 背后没有兵马，只有言语。

normal.en: Under threat means the pressure has already arrived.
normal.cn: under threat 意为压力已经临头。

normal.en: A storm, a virus or a rising sea can pose a threat, with no person involved.
normal.cn: 风暴、病毒或上涨的海面都能构威胁，其中没有人的身影。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that never comes down: the waiting is the threat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起却始终没落下的手：等待本身就是威胁。

abstract.en: A threat is danger that has learned to speak.
abstract.cn: 威胁是学会了说话的危险。

abstract.en: Threat is the shadow cast forward by something bad still on its way.
abstract.cn: 威胁是尚未到达的坏事提前投下的影子。

examples.en: The letter contained a threat to burn the warehouse.
examples.cn: 这封信里威胁要烧掉仓库。

examples.en: Pollution is the greatest threat to the river.
examples.cn: 污染是这条河最大的威胁。

examples.en: Nobody took his threat seriously.
examples.cn: 没人把他的威胁当真。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拽的」——被人死拽着衣领不让走，那种逼迫感 → threat 威胁

root: 古英语 þreat，源自日耳曼词根「压、挤、逼迫」，本兼指人群、队伍与压迫；中古英语收窄为敌对力量的危险，动词后由 threaten 承担。

sensesIntro.en: Threat keeps one image of pressure and moves it from spoken words to a feeling, a dangerous source and a sign in the sky.
sensesIntro.cn: threat 保持「压迫」这一个意象，从说出的话挪到一个感觉、一个危险源，以及天上的兆头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand that never falls, holding the air tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：举起却始终不落的手，让空气绷紧。

branches.en: The words: someone names the harm they will do.
branches.cn: 言语线：有人说出他将要施加的伤害。

branches.en: The feeling: pressure sensed before anything is said.
branches.cn: 感觉线：什么都没说，压力先被感到。

branches.en: The source: a virus, a sea or a person that endangers.
branches.cn: 源头线：病毒、海水或某个人构成危险。

branches.en: The sign: clouds or cracks that foretell harm.
branches.cn: 兆头线：预示伤害的乌云或裂缝。

branches.en: Said and unsaid pressure are the same word.
branches.cn: 说出的压力与未说出的压力是同一个词。

intro.en: Threat stays bare as a noun; the family grows through -en and -ing.
intro.cn: threat 作名词保持原形；词族通过 -en 与 -ing 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: He was a menace on the road.

definition_zh: 使复杂化；使难懂；使恶化
definition_en: to make something more difficult to understand or deal with
core_image: 本来一条笔直的线，被不断打结，越绕越乱
scene: 本来只是一件小事，他一解释反而添了乱。 Do not complicate a simple apology with long excuses.
sceneCN: 这里 complicate 指「使复杂化」（第 1 个义项：让事情变得更难处理）；句意是别用冗长的借口把一句简单的道歉弄复杂。

pos.zh: 使复杂化；使难懂；使恶化

senses.title: Make harder to follow
senses.definition: to make something harder to understand by adding parts
senses.definitionCN: 通过增加内容让某事更难理解
senses.example: Extra rules only complicate the game.
senses.exampleCN: 多余的规则只会让游戏变复杂。
senses.why: Every added part becomes one more thing the mind must hold.
senses.whyCN: 每增加一部分，脑子就要多记住一样东西。

senses.title: Make a problem worse
senses.definition: to make a bad situation or illness more serious
senses.definitionCN: 使糟糕的处境或病情变得更严重
senses.example: Stress can complicate recovery from illness.
senses.exampleCN: 压力会让病后恢复变得更棘手。
senses.why: A second trouble arriving on top of the first multiplies the burden.
senses.whyCN: 第二个麻烦压在第一个之上，负担就成倍增加。

senses.title: Twist things together
senses.definition: to fold or twist things together so they are hard to separate
senses.definitionCN: 把东西折叠或缠绕在一起，难以分开
senses.example: The wires were complicated into a tight knot.
senses.exampleCN: 电线被缠成了一个紧结。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical folding, and confusion is folding in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是物理上的折叠，而困惑就是脑子里的折叠。

intro.en: Complicate comes from Latin complicare, to fold together, and first described things twisted into one another.
intro.cn: complicate 来自拉丁语 complicare，意为折在一起，最初描述互相缠结的东西。

items.en: Com- meant together and plicare meant to fold.
items.cn: com- 表示一起，plicare 表示折叠。

items.en: Complicare described folding several layers into one bundle.
items.cn: complicare 描述把好几层折成一捆。

items.en: Old French compliquer carried the idea into everyday speech.
items.cn: 古法语 compliquer 把这个意思带入日常语言。

items.en: English complicate first meant to intertwine or entangle.
items.cn: 英语 complicate 最初指使交织、使缠结。

items.en: It now means to make a matter harder to understand or to handle.
items.cn: 如今它指让事情更难理解或更难处理。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that share the shape of complicate, and the meaning group names other ways of making a matter hard.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complicate 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他把事弄难的说法。

entries.definition: made of many connected parts
a problem that makes a situation worse
hard to understand or deal with
to make someone unable to think clearly
to twist things together so they are hard to separate
to make something confusing or disordered

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with folded cloth, then move to tangled wires and to problems that grow heavier.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从折起的布开始，再走到缠住的电线与越压越重的问题。

normal.en: Com- is together and plic- is fold, so to complicate is to fold things into each other.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，plic- 是折叠，所以 complicate 就是把东西折到一起。

normal.en: A simple task plus one extra rule equals a complicated task.
normal.cn: 简单的任务加一条多余的规则，就变成复杂的任务。

normal.en: A knot is complicate made visible in a piece of string.
normal.cn: 一个结，就是 complicate 在一根绳子上的可见形态。

normal.en: When an illness is complicated, a second problem has joined the first.
normal.cn: 病情被 complicate 时，就是第二个问题加入了第一个。

normal.en: Keep the promise simple and you never need to complicate it.
normal.cn: 把承诺保持简单，就永远不必把它弄复杂。

abstract.en: Picture one straight road that keeps splitting into smaller paths.
abstract.cn: 想象一条直路不断分出更小的岔路。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of string pulled by two hands at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一团线被两只手同时拉扯。

abstract.en: Picture a short answer buried under pages of notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个简短答案被成页的注释埋住。

examples.en: The new rules only complicate the process for everyone.
examples.cn: 新规则只是让每个人的流程都变复杂。

examples.en: Travel delays were complicated by heavy snow.
examples.cn: 旅途的延误因大雪而更加棘手。

examples.en: Please do not complicate matters with more forms.
examples.cn: 请不要再拿更多表格把事情弄复杂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complicate 记成 com（一起）加 plic（折叠）：把好几层折到一起，事情就变复杂了。

root: 源自拉丁语 complicare（com 一起 + plicare 折叠），本义是把东西折在一起，后引申为使事情交织、难懂与恶化。

sensesIntro.en: From folded cloth, to a tangled knot, and finally to a problem that grows heavier.
sensesIntro.cn: 从折起的布，到缠成的结，最后到越压越重的问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one straight line folded again and again until it is a knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条直线被反复折叠，最后成了一个结。

branches.en: Adding parts is the everyday way to complicate a task.
branches.cn: 增加内容是把任务弄复杂的日常方式。

branches.en: A second trouble makes the first one heavier.
branches.cn: 第二个麻烦会让第一个更沉重。

branches.en: The physical knot is the oldest picture behind the word.
branches.cn: 物理上的结，是这个词最古老的画面。

branches.en: Both senses add a layer that did not need to be there.
branches.cn: 两个义项都添了一层本不必要的负担。

branches.en: A tangled knot and a worsened problem both resist easy undoing.
branches.cn: 缠死的结与恶化的难题都难以轻松解开。

intro.en: Complicate is built on Latin com-, together, plus the base plic-, to fold.
intro.cn: complicate 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与词基 plic-（折叠）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin fold base plic- also appears in complex and multiply.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的折叠词基 plic- 也出现在 complex 与 multiply 中。

items.meaning: to make something harder to follow
items.exampleCN: 冗长的表格让申请变复杂。

items.example: The machine has a complicated design.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器的设计很复杂。
晚些时候出现了一个使情况恶化的因素。

items.example: The surgery had one small complication.
items.exampleCN: 手术出现了一个小并发症。

items.example: The brain is a complex organ.
items.exampleCN: 大脑是一个复杂的器官。

items.example: The complexity of the law surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 法律的复杂性让我们吃惊。

definition_en: a careful look at something to judge its condition, quality, or safety
core_image: 戴手套的人俯身贴近机器，用手电照着焊缝一寸寸看过去
scene: 车间里机器刚停下，一名佩戴证件的工作人员拿着手电靠近焊缝。 A careful inspection showed that the pipe had a small crack.
sceneCN: 这里 inspection 是「检查」（第 1 个义项：为判断状况、质量或安全而仔细查看），句意是仔细检查后发现管道上有一条细裂缝。画面里能看到的物件：手电、焊缝、证件。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干构成的后备动词，义为「检查；视察」
由本词换后缀构成，义为「检查员；督察」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「检查性质的」

senses.title: A careful examination
senses.definition: an official or careful look at something in order to find faults or judge quality
senses.definitionCN: 为找出问题或判断质量而进行的正式、仔细的查看
senses.example: The car passed inspection without a single fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车通过检查时没有任何故障。
senses.why: Latin specere means to look; inspection is the noun of looking into a thing closely.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 specere 意为「看」；inspection 就是凑近往里面看的那个动作的名词。

senses.title: An official visit to check
senses.definition: an official visit by an authority to check that rules are being followed
senses.definitionCN: 权力机构为核查规则是否被遵守而进行的正式到访
senses.example: The school prepares for inspection every second year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校每隔一年准备迎接视察。
senses.why: The look becomes institutional: someone with authority comes to see whether things are done correctly.
senses.whyCN: 这种「看」被制度化了：有权的人前来看事情是否做得对。

senses.title: The act of looking closely
senses.definition: the act of examining something closely with your own eyes, often to notice details
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的眼睛仔细查看某物，往往是为了发现细节
senses.example: On closer inspection, the painting turned out to be a copy.
senses.exampleCN: 细看之下，那幅画原来是仿作。
senses.why: The oldest and simplest sense: bending down to see what the eye misses at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老、最简单的义项：俯下身去看远处看不见的东西。

intro.en: Inspection is a Latin noun of action from inspicere "to look into", built on specere "to see".
intro.cn: inspection 是拉丁语 inspicere「向里看」的行为名词，基于 specere「看」。

items.en: Specere "to look at" was one of the basic verbs of seeing in Latin.
items.cn: specere「看」是拉丁语中最基本的视觉动词之一。

items.en: In- plus specere gave inspicere, "to look into, examine".
items.cn: in- 加 specere 得到 inspicere，意为「向里看、查察」。

items.en: The noun of action inspectio named the examination itself.
items.cn: 行为名词 inspectio 指查看这件事本身。

items.en: Old French passed inspection into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 inspection 传入英语。

items.en: Industrial and school inspection gave the word its official, regular sense.
items.cn: 工业检查与学校视察赋予了它官方、定期的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares Latin spec- "look"; the near-meaning group holds other words for examining.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 spec-「看」；近义组收其他表示「检查」的词。

entries.definition: Someone who watches, built on the same looking root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众」，用同一「看」词根构成。

entries.definition: To think someone is guilty, literally "to look up from below".
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，字面是「从下往上看」。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to look into closely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，是本词背后的动词，义为「仔细查看」。

entries.definition: A close testing look, wider and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审查」，范围更宽、更正式。

entries.definition: A quick test that looks right or works.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查」，强调快速确认是否正常。

entries.definition: An official examination of financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计」，指对财务记录的正式检查。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the root spec- "look" and the prepositions that go with the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词根 spec-「看」以及这个词常用的介词搭配。

normal.en: spec- is to look: inspection is looking in.
normal.cn: spec- 是「看」：inspection 就是往里看。

normal.en: Spectator, suspect and inspect all share the root.
normal.cn: spectator、suspect、inspect 共享词根。

normal.en: On inspection, the engine had two loose bolts.
normal.cn: 经检查，发动机上有两颗松动的螺栓。

normal.en: A safety inspection happens before a factory reopens.
normal.cn: 工厂复工前会做安全检查。

normal.en: Close inspection often finds what a quick glance misses.
normal.cn: 细看常能发现一眼扫过所遗漏的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a beam of light moving slowly along a seam.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光沿着接缝慢慢移动。

abstract.en: An inspection is a conversation between the eye and the object.
abstract.cn: 检查是眼睛与物件之间的一场对话。

abstract.en: What survives inspection deserves trust; what avoids it does not.
abstract.cn: 经得起检查的东西值得信任，躲避检查的不值得。

examples.en: The building failed its fire inspection.
examples.cn: 这座建筑未通过消防检查。

examples.en: On inspection, the letter proved to be false.
examples.cn: 经查看，那封信原来是伪造的。

examples.en: Officials made an inspection of the harbour.
examples.cn: 官员们对港口进行了视察。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯佩克」——按品牌要求一项项查看，就是检查

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」→ in- + specere = inspicere「向里看、查察」→ 行为名词 inspectio「检查」→ 古法语 → 十四世纪英语 inspection。spec-/spect- 也见于 spectacle、spectator、suspect、respect。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a careful examination, an official visit, and plain close looking.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：仔细检查、官方视察，以及朴素的「细看」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand guides a torch along a weld, inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴手套的手拿着手电沿着焊縫一寸寸照。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: a machine is checked for faults.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：检查机器有无故障。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: an authority visits to enforce rules.
branches.cn: 机关这条线：权力部门到访核查规则。

branches.en: THE GALLERY: a closer look changes what we think.
branches.cn: 画廊这条线：凑近细看改变了我们的判断。

branches.en: THE LINK: official and personal inspection both rest on looking closely.
branches.cn: 连接线：官方检查与个人细看都靠凑近看。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE: the official sense is regular and predictable.
branches.cn: 日程线：官方义是定期、可预期的。

intro.en: Inspection is in- "into" plus spec- "look", with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: inspection 是 in-「向内」加 spec-「看」，再加名词词尾 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere, inspicere and inspectio are attested, so no reconstruction is needed for this layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere、inspicere、inspectio 均有记载，这一层无需重构。

definition_zh: 引用；引述；报价；引语；报价单
definition_en: to repeat words from a text or speaker; to state a price for goods or work; words repeated from a source; a stated price
core_image: 录音笔倒回到开头，屏幕上是逐字对照的文稿
scene: 记者把录音倒回开头，逐字核对手稿里引用的那句话。 The reporter checked the words she planned to quote from the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 quote 是「引用、引述」（第 1 个义项：重复别人说过或写过的话）；句意为记者核对了她准备从采访中引用的那段话。画面里可留意：倒回的录音、逐字的文稿、圈出的句子。

collocations.zh: 所谓（口语，表示照搬别人的说法）

derivatives.zh: quote 加 -ation，指引语、引用行为或报价
mis- 加 quote，指错误地引用
un- 与 quote 相对，指结束引文，多用于 quote unquote 的口语说法

senses.title: To repeat another's words
senses.definition: to repeat the exact words that someone has said or written
senses.definitionCN: 逐字重复别人说过或写过的话
senses.example: She quoted a line from the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她引用了报告里的一句话。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word meant to mark a passage with a number, and later to read it out with a marker, which is what citation is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁语动词本指给某段落标上编号，后来指标记着朗读，这正是引用的动作。

senses.title: To state a price
senses.definition: to tell a customer in advance how much goods or work will cost
senses.definitionCN: 事先告诉顾客货物或工作要花多少钱
senses.example: The garage quoted three hundred pounds for the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 修车行对这单维修报了三百英镑。
senses.why: A merchant who marks a price on goods is marking a figure for the buyer, the same marking verb used for texts.
senses.whyCN: 商人在货物上标价，就是为买家标出一个数字，与给文本标号用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: Words repeated from a source
senses.definition: a passage repeated from a book, speech or interview, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 从书、演讲或采访中取来重复的一段话，作名词用
senses.example: He put a quote from the coach on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他把教练的一句话贴在墙上。
senses.why: English speakers shortened quotation to quote, and the shorter form kept the meaning of the cited passage.
senses.whyCN: 英语使用者把 quotation 缩略为 quote，这个较短的形式保留了「被引段落」的意思。

senses.title: A stated price
senses.definition: a price given in writing or in speech before work begins, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 在工作开始前以书面或口头给出的价格，作名词用
senses.example: The quote came in higher than we expected.
senses.exampleCN: 报价比我们预想的高。
senses.why: The verb to quote a price produced a noun quote for the figure itself, common in building and insurance work.
senses.whyCN: 动词「报价」产生了名词 quote，指那个价格数字本身，在建筑与保险行业很常见。

intro.en: Quote is the shortened form of quotation, and both go back to a Latin verb of numbering and marking that came to English through French.
intro.cn: quote 是 quotation 的缩略形式，两者都可追溯到拉丁语中表示编号与标记的动词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quot meant how many and appeared in the numbering of chapters and lines.
items.cn: quot 意为多少，出现在给章节与诗行编号的用法中。

items.en: Quotare meant to mark a book with numbers so that a passage could be found and cited.
items.cn: quotare 意为用数字标记书本，以便找到并引证某段。

items.en: Old French quoter kept the sense of marking and citing, and also of setting a price.
items.cn: 古法语 quoter 保留了标记与引证的意思，也指定价。

items.en: Middle English used quote for citing and for stating a price, two senses that still stand side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quote 既指引证，也指定价，这两层意思至今并列。

items.en: Modern English shortened quotation to quote, especially in speech, journalism and trade.
items.cn: 现代英语把 quotation 缩略为 quote，尤其在口语、新闻与商贸中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin stem of numbering; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of citing, repeating and pricing.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「编号」词干上的形式；近义组收表示引用、重复与定价的动词。

entries.definition: Cited words, or a price given in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 被引用的话，或预先给出的价格。

entries.definition: Worth repeating in another text.
entries.definitionCN: 值得在别的文本中重复的。

entries.definition: A fixed share assigned to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给一个群体的固定份额。

entries.definition: The number produced by division.
To mention a source formally, especially in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提到一个来源，尤指在写作中。

entries.definition: To say or do something again.
To give an approximate figure in advance.
To set the amount of money asked for something.

normalIntro.en: The word marks a passage or a price: both are figures set out for others to read, repeat or accept.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词标记一段话或一个价格：两者都是摆出来供别人阅读、重复或接受的数字。

normal.en: Quote is a shortened quotation, so the noun and the verb look exactly alike.
normal.cn: quote 是 quotation 的缩略，所以名词和动词长得一模一样。

normal.en: Quote unquote is the spoken way of putting quotation marks around someone else's phrase.
normal.cn: quote unquote 是口语中给别人的说法加上引号的方式。

normal.en: A builder's quote is a price marked on paper, using the same verb as quoting a sentence.
normal.cn: 施工方的 quote 是写在纸上的价格，用的动词与引用一句话相同。

normal.en: To quote someone on a subject is to report their exact words about it.
normal.cn: quote someone on 某话题，就是报告他们对这个话题的原话。

normal.en: Misquote means to get the words wrong, and it is one of the commonest complaints in journalism.
normal.cn: misquote 意为引错话，是新闻业最常见的投诉之一。

abstract.en: To quote well is to disappear for a moment and let the other voice be heard clearly.
abstract.cn: 引得好，就是让自己暂时消失，让另一个声音被清楚地听见。

abstract.en: A price quoted in advance is a promise about the future, which is why a quote can feel like a commitment.
abstract.cn: 预先报出的价格是对未来的一个承诺，所以 quote 会让人觉得像一种约定。

abstract.en: Quoting and pricing both fix a number in place, one on a page and one on a market.
abstract.cn: 引用与定价都是把一个数字固定下来，一个固定在纸页上，一个固定在市场上。

examples.en: She quoted the contract exactly in her letter.
examples.cn: 她在信里一字不差地引用了合同。

examples.en: The shop quoted me a lower price for the same chair.
examples.cn: 同一把椅子，这家店给我报的价更低。

examples.en: He wrote the coach's quote on a card above his desk.
examples.cn: 他把教练的那句话写在一张卡片上，贴到书桌上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔特」——阔气地把别人的话原样搬来，记得标出处，记住 quote 是引用。

root: 拉丁语 quot（多少）→ 中世纪拉丁语 quotare（编号、标记）→ 古法语 quoter → 英语 quote；同族有 quotation、quota、quotient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a marked figure; the senses divide into repeating words, setting a price, the repeated words themselves and the price itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被标出的数字或段落」；义项分为重复他人的话、定出价格、被重复的话本身，以及价格本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder wound back to the start, beside a word-for-word transcript.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒回开头的录音笔，旁边放着逐字对照的文稿。

branches.en: a finger tracing one line twice
branches.cn: 手指把一行字描了两遍

branches.en: a figure written on an order form
branches.cn: 写在订单上的一个数字

branches.en: a sentence framed on a wall
branches.cn: 被框起来挂在墙上的一句话

branches.en: a sum circled at the bottom of a letter
branches.cn: 信末被圈出的金额

branches.en: the act of quoting and the thing quoted
branches.cn: 引用的动作与被引用之物

intro.en: The word is a shortened French borrowing on the Latin root of numbering, with English endings that build nouns, adjectives and negative verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「编号」词根上的法语缩略借词，加上构成名词、形容词与否定动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem quot- also gave quota and quotient, which keep the plain idea of a counted share.
latinIntro.cn: quot- 这个词干还给出了 quota 与 quotient，它们保留了「被计算出的份额」这一朴素意思。

definition_en: relating to society, to meeting other people, or to living in groups
core_image: 公园里人们三五成群地交谈
scene: 住房是重要的社会问题。 Housing is an important social issue.
sceneCN: 这里 social 是「社会的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：住房是重要的社会问题。

senses.title: Of society
senses.definition: relating to society and the way people live together
senses.definitionCN: 与社会以及人们共同生活的方式相关的
senses.example: Housing is an important social issue.
senses.exampleCN: 住房是重要的社会问题。
senses.why: This is the broad sense covering public life.
senses.whyCN: 这是涵盖公共生活的宽泛义项。

senses.title: Of meeting people
senses.definition: relating to meeting friends and spending time with others
senses.definitionCN: 与见朋友、与他人共度时光相关的
senses.example: She has a busy social life.
senses.exampleCN: 她的社交生活很忙。
senses.why: The word also names personal contact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指个人之间的交往。

senses.title: Living in groups
senses.definition: living in groups rather than alone
senses.definitionCN: 成群生活而非独居的
senses.example: Bees are social insects.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂是群居昆虫。
senses.why: Biology uses the word for group living.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个词表示群体生活。

intro.cn: social 来自拉丁语 socius，意为同伴。

items.en: Socialis meant belonging to companions.

items.en: The word entered English for life in company.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，表示与人相处的生活。

items.en: It widened to the whole of public life.

items.en: Science used it for animals that live in groups.
items.cn: 科学用这个词指群居动物。

abstract.en: A society is a promise people make to strangers.

abstract.en: We learn ourselves through other people.

definition_en: to believe someone may be guilty, or a person thought to be guilty
core_image: 警探在灯下翻看档案，目光停在一个人名上
scene: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。 The police suspect that he hid the money.
sceneCN: 这里 suspect 是「怀疑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。

senses.title: To believe someone is guilty
senses.definition: to think that someone may be guilty or dishonest
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人可能有罪或不诚实
senses.example: The police suspect that he hid the money.
senses.exampleCN: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。
senses.why: This is the core sense of suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 这是「怀疑」的核心义项。

senses.title: A person believed guilty

senses.definitionCN: 被认为犯了罪的人

senses.why: As a noun the word names the person.

senses.title: Likely to be bad or false

senses.definitionCN: 可能是坏的、假的或危险的

senses.why: As an adjective it describes things that raise doubt.

definition_en: money that people must pay to the government, or to make someone pay or work hard
core_image: 账本上一行被划走的分量
scene: 市里提高了停车税，车主们纷纷抱怨。 The city raised the tax on parking, and drivers complained.
sceneCN: 这里 tax 是「税」（第 1 个义项）；句意：市里提高了停车税，车主们纷纷抱怨。

senses.title: Money paid to the state
senses.definition: money that people or businesses must pay to the government
senses.definitionCN: 个人或企业必须向政府缴纳的钱
senses.example: The city raised the tax on parking.
senses.exampleCN: 市里提高了停车税。
senses.why: The root meant to assess and rate a value, and the assessed sum became the tax.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为评估、核定价值，被核定出的那一笔钱就成了税。

senses.title: To impose a tax
senses.definition: to make someone pay a tax on something
senses.definitionCN: 要求某人为某物缴税
senses.example: The government taxed tobacco heavily.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对烟草课以重税。
senses.why: Assessing a value led to the act of charging it.
senses.whyCN: 核定价值这一动作，发展成实际征收。

senses.title: To put a strain on someone
senses.definition: to make heavy demands on someone's strength or patience
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的体力或耐心提出很高要求
senses.example: The long journey taxed his patience.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的旅程考验了他的耐心。
senses.why: A tax takes a share of what you have, just as strain takes a share of your strength.
senses.whyCN: 税拿走你的一部分钱财，正如负担拿走你的一部分力气。

intro.en: Tax goes back to a Latin verb meaning to assess or appraise.
intro.cn: tax 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「评估、核定」的动词。

items.en: Taxare meant to assess and appraise.
items.cn: taxare 意为评估、核定。

items.en: Taxa meant an assessed charge.
items.cn: taxa 意为核定出的费用。

items.en: Taxer meant to charge or blame.
items.cn: taxer 意为征收或指责。

items.en: Tax meant a sum demanded by a ruler.
items.cn: tax 指统治者要求缴纳的款项。

items.en: Tax extended to strain and to blame.
items.cn: tax 扩展到「使负累」与「指责」。

note.en: Tax is compared with look-alike words and with words for charges and burdens.
note.cn: 把 tax 与形近词以及表示费用与负担的词作对比。

a car you pay to ride in
a plural of taxi or a medical term
a tax on goods
an amount charged officially
a heavy load

normalIntro.en: Tax is a share assessed and taken from what you own.
normalIntro.cn: tax 是从你的所得中被核定并取走的一份。

normal.en: The city raised the tax on parking.
normal.cn: 市里提高了停车税。

normal.en: The government taxed tobacco heavily.
normal.cn: 政府对烟草课以重税。

normal.en: The long journey taxed his patience.

normal.en: He filed his tax return in April.
normal.cn: 他在四月提交了纳税申报。

normal.en: Small shops often struggle with high taxes.
normal.cn: 小店常被高税负拖累。

abstract.en: A tax is a measured slice taken away.
abstract.cn: 税是被量好切走的一片。

abstract.en: To be taxed is to lend strength to a purpose.
abstract.cn: 被征税就是把力气借给某个目的。

abstract.en: Even patience can be taxed.
abstract.cn: 连耐心也会被课税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踏克斯」——每走一步都要「踏」出一份钱，就是交税。

root: 拉丁语 taxare（评估、核定）经中世纪拉丁语 taxa 与古法语 taxer 进入英语，由「核定的钱」转为「税」。

sensesIntro.en: Tax starts as an assessed sum, becomes the act of charging it, then any heavy demand.
sensesIntro.cn: tax 从核定的一笔钱，变成征收动作，再到任何沉重的要求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measured share cut from a pile.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一堆里量出的一份被切走。

branches.en: The payment is the main sense.
branches.cn: 税款是主要义项。

branches.en: Charging it is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 征收是动词义。

branches.en: Strain takes strength like tax takes money.
branches.cn: 负担取走力气，如同税收取走钱财。

branches.en: Sum and charge are one system.
branches.cn: 款项与征收是一套制度。

branches.en: Patience can be charged too.
branches.cn: 耐心也能被课税。

intro.en: Tax builds taxation, taxable, and taxpayer.
intro.cn: tax 构成 taxation、taxable、taxpayer。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare, to assess, is the direct source of the tax family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 taxare（评估）是 tax 词族的直接来源。

definition_en: to think or believe; to calculate or estimate; to count on something; to settle an account
core_image: 渔夫坐在船头，用手指节在木板上比划数目
scene: 渔夫坐在船头，凭经验数着今天的收获。 I reckon it will rain before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 reckon 是「认为」（第 1 个义项：觉得、估计）；句意为我认为中午前会下雨。画面里可留意：船头数收成的渔夫、比划的手指。

senses.title: To think or believe
senses.definition: to think that something is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事为真或很可能发生
senses.example: I reckon it will rain before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为中午前会下雨。
senses.why: Counting a thing as true became the everyday sense of believing, because a judgment is a sum we make in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 把一件事算作真的，就成了日常的「相信」，因为判断正是心里做的一次加法。

senses.title: To calculate or estimate
senses.definition: to work out an amount by counting or judging
senses.definitionCN: 通过数算或判断算出某个数量
senses.example: The builder reckoned the cost at ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方估算成本为一万英镑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to count in order, and adding up numbers is still the clearest use of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是按顺序数算，而把数字加起来仍是这个动词最清楚的用法。

senses.title: To count on something
senses.definition: to rely on something happening or being available
senses.definitionCN: 依赖某事发生或可得到
senses.example: We reckoned on fine weather for the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们指望野餐时天气晴好。
senses.why: To reckon on is to put something into your sum as certain, and hope is a kind of accounting.
senses.whyCN: reckon on 就是把某件事当作确定的项计入你的账里，而期待本身就是一种算计。

senses.title: To settle an account
senses.definition: to work out and settle what is owed between people
senses.definitionCN: 算出并结清人与人之间应付的款项
senses.example: The clerk reckoned the bill at the end of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 店员在一天结束时结清了账目。
senses.why: A reckoning is the moment when the numbers are finally added and the account is closed.
senses.whyCN: reckoning 就是数字终于加完、账目就此结清的时刻。

intro.en: Reckon is a native English verb of recounting: telling in order, counting in order, and finally judging.
intro.cn: reckon 是英语本族表「讲述」的动词：按顺序讲述，按顺序数算，最后成为判断。

items.en: Gerecenian meant to recount or explain, telling a matter in order.
items.cn: gerecenian 意为讲述或解释，把事情按顺序说出来。

items.en: From recounting came the sense of counting and adding up amounts.
items.cn: 从「讲述」引申出「数算」与「加总」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reknen meant both to count and to think.
items.cn: 中古英语 reknen 既指数算，也指思考。

items.en: Counting something as true became the everyday sense of believing.
items.cn: 把某事算作真的，成为日常的「相信」。

items.en: Modern English uses reckon for thinking, estimating, relying, and settling accounts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reckon 表认为、估算、指望与结账。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of thinking, counting, and estimating.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的短词；近义组收表思考、计算与估算的动词。

entries.definition: To signal someone to come.
A small sign or voucher.
Acting without care.
To hold an opinion.
To work out by numbers.
To assume something is true.
To judge an amount roughly.

normalIntro.en: The word began as telling in order, became counting in order, and ended as judging in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从按顺序讲述开始，变为按顺序数算，最后成为心里的判断。

normal.en: Reckon sounds like reckoning: adding numbers until a total appears.
normal.cn: reckon 与 reckoning 同源：一直加数，直到总数出现。

normal.en: I reckon is the spoken way to say I think.
normal.cn: I reckon 是口语里的「我认为」。

normal.en: Reckon with means to take something into your sum.
normal.cn: reckon with 意为把某事计入你的账里。

normal.en: Reckon on means to rely on it being there.
normal.cn: reckon on 意为指望它在。

normal.en: Reckon up the bill is to add all the items together.
normal.cn: reckon up the bill 就是把所有项目加起来。

abstract.en: To reckon is to make the world add up, even when the numbers resist.
abstract.cn: 估算就是让世界加得起来，即使数字并不配合。

abstract.en: Every reckoning is a moment when someone decides what counts.
abstract.cn: 每一次清算，都是某人决定「什么才算数」的时刻。

abstract.en: Reckless people refuse the sum that others cannot stop making.
abstract.cn: 鲁莽的人拒绝去做别人停不下来的那道加法。

examples.en: I reckon it will rain before noon.
examples.cn: 我认为中午前会下雨。

examples.en: The builder reckoned the cost at ten thousand pounds.
examples.cn: 施工方估算成本为一万英镑。

examples.en: We reckoned on fine weather for the picnic.
examples.cn: 我们指望野餐时天气晴好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「渔夫用指节在船板上数数」：数着数着，心里就有了判断——认为、估算都由此而来。

root: 古英语 gerecenian（讲述、数算）→ 中古英语 reknen → 现代英语 reckon；同族有 reckoning、reckless。

sensesIntro.en: The core is counting in order; the senses move from calculation to expectation, to judgment, and to a settled account.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按序数算」；义项从计算，到期待，到判断，再到结清的账目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fisherman at the bow counting his catch on the planks.
core.cn: 核心意象：渔夫坐在船头，在木板上数着收成。

branches.en: a fisherman guessing the weather
branches.cn: 渔夫猜测天气

branches.en: a builder's estimate on paper
branches.cn: 施工方写在纸上的估算

branches.en: a picnic planned on fine weather
branches.cn: 指望晴天而安排的野餐

branches.en: a bill settled at the day's end
branches.cn: 一天结束时结清的账单

branches.en: a judgment reached and an amount worked out
branches.cn: 得出的判断与算出的数目

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its small family is built on the idea of counting and on the suffix that turns it into a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其不大的词族建立在「数算」的观念与把它名词化的后缀上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded; reckon is a native Germanic verb.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；reckon 是日耳曼语本族动词。

definition_zh: 全部的；整个的；完整无缺的
definition_en: whole, with no part missing or left out
core_image: 一块布从一头铺到另一头，没有一处缺口
scene: 大雪下了整整一夜，第二天整个村子都白了。 Snow fell all night, and the entire village was white by morning.
sceneCN: 这里 entire 是「整个的」（第 1 个义项：完整无缺的全部）；句意：雪下了一整夜，到早晨整个村子都白了。

pos.zh: 全部的；整个的；完整无缺的

senses.title: Whole, with nothing left out
senses.definition: including every part of something, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 包含某物的每一部分，没有遗漏
senses.example: The entire class passed the test.
senses.exampleCN: 全班都通过了考试。
senses.why: The Latin root means untouched and whole, so the adjective names a thing with no part removed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「未被触碰、完整」，所以这个形容词指没有去掉任何部分的事物。

senses.title: Complete and unbroken
senses.definition: still in one piece, not damaged or divided
senses.definitionCN: 仍为一体，没有损坏或分裂
senses.example: The ancient wall is still entire after two thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 两千年后，这堵古墙依然完整。
senses.why: The original sense of untouched survives in the idea of something whole and undamaged.
senses.whyCN: 「未被触碰」的原义，保留在「完整无损」这一含义中。

senses.title: Complete in degree
senses.definition: complete or total in an abstract sense, such as trust or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在抽象意义上完全、彻底，如信任或一致
senses.example: He had the entire confidence of the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他拥有董事会的完全信任。
senses.why: Whole applied to abstract things means complete and unreserved.
senses.whyCN: 「整体」用于抽象事物，就表示完全、毫无保留。

intro.en: Entire comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成，经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Middle English entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: Modern English uses entire mainly for the whole of something.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entire 主要用于表示某事物的全部。

note.en: Entire is a wholeness word, and it sits near its family and near words for whole and complete.
note.cn: entire 是一个「完整」词，与自身词族以及表示全部和完整的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Entire comes from Latin integer, untouched or whole, so the word pictures something with no part removed.
normalIntro.cn: entire 来自拉丁语 integer（未被触碰、完整），所以这个词描绘没有去掉任何部分的事物。

normal.en: Integer means whole, and it also gives us the mathematical integer.
normal.cn: integer 意为完整，也给我们数学中的「整数」。

normal.en: The entire day means all of it, with nothing left out.
normal.cn: the entire day 指一整天，没有遗漏。

normal.en: The adverb entirely means completely.
normal.cn: 副词 entirely 表示完全地。

normal.en: The noun entirety appears in the phrase in its entirety.
normal.cn: 名词 entirety 出现在短语 in its entirety 中。

normal.en: Compare whole: whole is plainer, while entire is slightly more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 whole：whole 更朴素，entire 稍正式。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with no corner torn away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸没有任何一角被撕掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a circle closed without the smallest gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆闭合得没有一丝缺口。

abstract.en: Think of a house lit from every window at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子的每扇窗同时亮起。

examples.en: The entire class passed the test.
examples.cn: 全班都通过了考试。

examples.en: She read the entire report in one sitting.
examples.cn: 她一口气读完了整份报告。

examples.en: The entire village came to the wedding.
examples.cn: 全村人都来参加婚礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——一条轮胎也没有漏掉，就是完整无缺的全部；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺的）→ 古法语 entier → 中古英语 entire，核心义「未被触碰、完整」。

sensesIntro.en: The word keeps the old sense of untouched wholeness, then extends it to physical completeness and finally to complete trust or agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词保留「未被触碰的完整」这一古老含义，再扩展到物理上的完好，最后用于完全的信任或一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Including every part is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 包含每一部分，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Physical soundness keeps the original untouched idea.
branches.cn: 物理上的完好保留原初「未被触碰」的意思。

branches.en: Complete trust applies wholeness to abstract things.
branches.cn: 完全的信任把「整体」用于抽象事物。

branches.en: Something whole in quantity is often also whole in condition.
branches.cn: 数量上完整的东西，状况上往往也完好。

branches.en: The whole of a thing can be given completely or trusted fully.
branches.cn: 事物的整体可以被完整给出，也可以被完全信任。

intro.en: Entire is a Latin adjective reshaped by French, and its English family grows with -ly, -ty, and -ness.
intro.cn: entire 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，英语词族由 -ly、-ty 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.exampleCN: in- 在 integer 中否定 tangere。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.

entirely 表示在每一部分上。

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
