definition_en: a picture of someone or something, or the idea that people have of a person or a company
core_image: 橱窗里一张被灯光打亮的人物海报
scene: 地铁通道的灯箱一夜之间全换了内容。 The image of a smiling farmer held the same pose on every panel, so commuters looked twice.
sceneCN: 这里 image 是「影像、图像」（第 1 个义项：人或物的画面），句意是一位微笑农夫的照片在每个灯箱上都保持同一姿势，乘客忍不住多看两眼。画面里有地铁通道和发亮的灯箱。

pos.zh: 名词：形象、影像、图像；印象

senses.title: A picture of something
senses.definition: a picture produced by a camera, a screen or a mirror
senses.definitionCN: 由相机、屏幕或镜子形成的画面
senses.example: The screen showed a sharp image of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上出现了清晰的月球影像。
senses.why: The word entered English as a name for a copy of a thing, a shape standing in for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，本是指某物的复制之形，即代替实物存在的那个样子。

senses.title: The idea people have of someone
senses.definition: the impression that a person or organisation gives to the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或机构给公众留下的总体观感
senses.example: The firm hired a designer to rebuild its image.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘请设计师重塑形象。
senses.why: The picture in public minds is treated as if it were a picture on a wall, so the same noun serves for fame and reputation.
senses.whyCN: 公众心中的那幅画被当成挂在墙上的画，于是同一个名词也用来指声望与口碑。

senses.title: A word picture in art and poetry
senses.definition: a description or figure of speech that makes readers see something
senses.definitionCN: 让读者眼前浮现画面的描写或修辞
senses.example: The poem opens with an image of rain on an empty road.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗以空荡路上下雨的意象开篇。
senses.why: Literature borrows the visual word because a good phrase paints a picture inside the reader.
senses.whyCN: 文学借用这个视觉词，因为一句好话能在读者心里画出图来。

intro.en: Image comes from a Latin word for a likeness or a statue, and it still keeps that sense of a shape standing for something.
intro.cn: image 来自拉丁语中表示「相似之物、雕像」的词，至今仍保留「以形代物」的含义。

items.en: Imago was a likeness, whether a carved statue or the picture of a face.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 指相像之物，既可为雕像，也可为面容的图画。

items.en: Imaginem was the accusative form most often met in texts, and it gave the word to later languages.
items.cn: 宾格形式 imaginem 在文献中最常见，后来的语言正是从这里取词。

items.en: French shortened it to image, still meaning a copy or a figure.
items.cn: 法语把它缩为 image，仍指复制之形或人物形象。

items.en: English adopted the French form and used it for statues, paintings and pictures in the mind.
items.cn: 英语沿用此形，用来指雕像、绘画以及心中的画面。

items.en: Photography and later television widened it to any picture made by light or by a screen.
items.cn: 摄影与后来的电视把它扩展到一切由光或屏幕生成的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same imag- root; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns for pictures.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 imag- 为词根的词；近义组收其他表示画面的名词。

entries.definition: To form a picture in the mind, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中构出画面，同一词根。

entries.definition: Images as a group, especially in art or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 图像或意象的集合，尤用于艺术与文学。

entries.definition: A copy of something, built on a similar pattern though not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 仿制品，构词形式相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: A painting, drawing or photograph, the plainest everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画、图画或照片，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: An image made by light on film or a sensor.
entries.definitionCN: 由光线落在胶片或传感器上形成的影像。

entries.definition: The opinion others hold of a person, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 他人对某人的评价，与第二个义项相近。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the Latin statue imago to screens, mirrors and public faces.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语的雕像 imago 连到屏幕、镜子和公众面孔上。

normal.en: Drop the final e and you get imag-, the root that also grows imagine and imagery.
normal.cn: 去掉词尾的 e 得到 imag-，这个词根还长出 imagine 与 imagery。

normal.en: Six letters, stress the first: IM-age.
normal.cn: 六个字母，重音在前：IM-age。

normal.en: Soft g at the end, so it rhymes with village, not with cage.
normal.cn: 结尾的 g 发软音，与 village 押韵，而不与 cage 同音。

normal.en: A mirror gives a mirror image, and a screen gives a digital image; the word is always a copy.
normal.cn: 镜子给出镜像，屏幕给出数字图像；这个词始终是复制品。

normal.en: Companies worry about their image just as cameras worry about theirs: both are pictures seen by others.
normal.cn: 公司操心形象，正如镜头操心成像：都是别人看见的那幅画。

abstract.en: An image is never the thing itself; it is the thing seen from outside, frozen long enough to be looked at.
abstract.cn: 图像从不是事物本身，而是事物从外部被看见、并被冻住足够久以供注视的样子。

abstract.en: The word holds both a mirror and a reputation, because people build a picture of you and then live beside it.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装着一面镜子和一份名声，因为人们先为你画像，再与那幅画同住。

abstract.en: Every picture is a small promise that a thing can be held still, and every failure of that promise disappoints us.
abstract.cn: 每幅画都是一个小承诺：事物可以被定住；这个承诺一旦落空，我们就会失望。

examples.en: The telescope sent back clear images of the planet.
examples.cn: 望远镜传回了这颗行星的清晰图像。

examples.en: Her public image as a strict judge is not quite fair.
examples.cn: 她作为严苛法官的公众形象并不太公允。

examples.en: He tried to improve the image of the brand after the scandal.
examples.cn: 丑闻之后他设法改善这个品牌的形象。

dict_mnemonic.text: imag 像（拉丁语「雕像、形貌」）+ e——照出来的样子，即影像；别人心中的样子，即形象

root: 拉丁语 imago（宾格 imaginem）「相似之物、雕像」，经古法语 image 进入英语，现代扩展到摄影图像与公众形象。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a visible picture, the picture held in public opinion, and a word picture in art.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：可见的画面、舆论中持有的印象，以及文学艺术中语言绘出的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit poster of a face repeated along a subway wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：地铁墙上被灯照亮、反复出现的同一张面孔。

branches.en: THE LENS LINE: cameras, screens and mirrors all produce images.
branches.cn: 镜头线：相机、屏幕与镜子都在产生图像。

branches.en: THE BRAND LINE: a company's image is its face in public.
branches.cn: 品牌线：公司的形象就是它在公众面前的脸。

branches.en: THE PAGE LINE: poets build images out of plain words.
branches.cn: 纸页线：诗人用朴素的词造出意象。

branches.en: THE COPY LINE: both are pictures standing in for something else.
branches.cn: 复制线：两者都是以画代物的复制。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: whether on glass or in lines of verse, the target is the eye.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：无论印在玻璃上还是写在诗句里，目标都是眼睛。

intro.en: Image is a Latin root with a light English ending; its family spreads across verbs, adjectives and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: image 是拉丁语词根加轻巧的英语词尾，其家族遍及动词、形容词与抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Imago and its stem imagin- are recorded in classical Latin, so the family rests on solid ground.
latinIntro.cn: imago 及其词干 imagin- 在古典拉丁语中都有文献，这个家族根基扎实。

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 imagery 中。

items.example: The film is full of strong images.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片充满强烈的意象。
她的想象力填补了空白。

items.example: The poem's imagery is all water.

items.exampleCN: 他们试了所有想得到的方法。

definition_en: the soft side of the face below the eye, or bold rudeness that shows no shame
core_image: 笑起来鼓起的两侧脸颊
scene: 屋里忽然安静下来，孩子低着头。 A tear ran down her cheek when she heard the news.
sceneCN: 这里 cheek 指「脸颊」（第 1 个义项：眼睛下方的面部侧面）；句意是她听到消息时一滴泪顺着脸颊流了下来。

collocations.zh: 挨了打还把另一边脸转过去

senses.title: The side of the face
senses.definition: the soft part of the face on either side below the eye
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛下方脸两侧柔软的部分
senses.example: A tear rolled down his cheek.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴泪顺着他的脸颊滚落。
senses.why: Old English used the word for the jaw, and the meaning later moved to the soft side of the face.
senses.whyCN: 古英语用这个词指颌骨，后来意义移到面部柔软的一侧。

senses.title: Bold rudeness
senses.definition: rude boldness that shows no shame or respect
senses.definitionCN: 毫无羞耻与敬意的放肆无礼
senses.example: He had the cheek to ask for more money.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟然有脸再要钱。
senses.why: A person without shame does not blush, so the word for the face came to mean impudence.
senses.whyCN: 不知羞耻的人不会脸红，于是表示「脸」的词也用来表示放肆。

intro.en: Cheek began as a word for the jaw and slid upward to the soft side of the face.
intro.cn: cheek 起初指颌骨，后来向上移到面部柔软的一侧。

items.en: A root kau- named the jaw and the act of chewing.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kau- 指颌骨与咀嚼的动作。

items.en: Ceace named the jaw and the bony side of the face.
items.cn: 古英语 ceace 指颌骨与面部骨性的一侧。

items.en: Cheke shifted to the soft flesh below the eye.
items.cn: cheke 的意义移到眼睛下方的柔软皮肉。

items.en: The word gained a second sense of bold rudeness.
items.cn: 这个词获得了「放肆无礼」的第二个义项。

items.en: Cheek now covers anatomy, manners and many fixed phrases.
items.cn: 如今 cheek 涵盖身体部位、举止以及大量固定搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same opening sound, while the meaning group names the face and boldness.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的开头音，近义组列出面部与放肆的说法。

entries.definition: to examine something closely
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食物

entries.definition: low in price or poor in quality
either of the bones that hold the teeth
boldness that others find rude
entries.definitionCN: 被别人视为无礼的大胆

entries.definition: fearless rudeness

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw root, the chewing link and the idiom about turning the other cheek.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌骨词根、咀嚼联系以及「转过另一边脸」的习语。

normal.en: Cheek once meant jaw, and the jaw muscle moves whenever you chew.
normal.cn: cheek 曾指颌骨，而咀嚼时动的正是颌部的肌肉。

normal.en: The plural cheeks simply adds an s to the soft side of the face.
normal.cn: 复数 cheeks 只是在表示面颊的词后加 s。

normal.en: Turn the other cheek is the famous phrase: it means to answer harm with patience.
normal.cn: turn the other cheek 是著名说法，意为以忍耐回应伤害。

normal.en: Cheek to cheek describes two dancers held close together.
normal.cn: cheek to cheek 形容两个舞者贴得很近。

normal.en: The same word turns abstract in have the cheek, which means to be boldly rude.
normal.cn: 同一个词在 have the cheek 中变得抽象，意为厚着脸皮。

abstract.en: Picture two red patches on a child's face after a long run.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子长跑之后脸上两团红。

abstract.en: Picture a tear stopping halfway down a still face.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴泪停在静止的脸颊中间。

abstract.en: Picture someone smiling calmly after being refused twice.
abstract.cn: 想象某人被拒绝两次后仍平静地笑着。

examples.en: Her cheeks went red when the teacher praised her.
examples.cn: 老师表扬她时，她的脸颊红了。

examples.en: He kissed his mother on the cheek and left.
examples.cn: 他亲了亲母亲的脸颊就走了。

examples.en: She had the cheek to blame the whole team.
examples.cn: 她竟有脸把责任推给整个团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheek 与 chew 同源：咀嚼时一鼓一鼓的地方，就是脸颊。

root: 源自日耳曼语词根 kau-（颌骨、咀嚼），古英语作 ceace，中古英语 cheke 转指眼睛下方的面颊。

sensesIntro.en: The jaw word climbs to the soft side of the face, and from the face it reaches the idea of shameless boldness.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示颌骨的词上移到面部柔软处，再由「脸」引申出不知羞耻的放肆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the soft curve of a face beside the smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：笑容旁边那一道柔软的脸部弧线。

branches.en: The physical cheek sits below the eye.
branches.cn: 实体的脸颊位于眼睛下方。

branches.en: The abstract sense names bold disrespect.
branches.cn: 抽象义指大胆无礼。

branches.en: Kissing on the cheek marks affection.
branches.cn: 亲脸颊表示亲近。

branches.en: The face word lends itself to idioms about shame.
branches.cn: 表示脸的词自然延伸出关于羞耻的习语。

branches.en: Having the cheek means lacking all shame.
branches.cn: have the cheek 意为毫无羞耻。

intro.en: Cheek builds a small family from one Old English stem.
intro.cn: cheek 由一个古英语词干构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic rather than Latin, and it links to the word for chewing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，并与表示咀嚼的词相连。

items.example: Her cheek was warm to the touch.
items.exampleCN: 她的脸颊摸上去是温的。

items.example: His cheeks were red from the cold.

items.exampleCN: 那个调皮的男孩顶了嘴。

items.meaning: in a rude but playful way
items.example: He grinned cheekily at the guard.

items.meaning: to crush food with the teeth

latinEntries.example: Ceace is the oldest recorded form of cheek.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ceace 是 cheek 有记录的最古形式。

definition_zh: 使恼怒；使烦恼；打扰；纠缠；使不适
definition_en: to make someone feel slightly angry or irritated, especially by repeated or unwanted actions
core_image: 一只小虫在耳边绕来绕去，赶走又回来
scene: 图书馆里，邻座的人不停翻动塑料包装，声音在安静中格外刺耳。 The repeated rustling began to annoy everyone at the long table.
sceneCN: 这里 annoy 是「使恼怒、使心烦」（第 1 个义项：反复的小干扰让人恼火）；句意为反复的窸窣声开始让长桌旁所有人都心烦。画面里有安静的图书馆、塑料包装与皱眉的读者。

pos.zh: 动词：使恼怒；使烦恼；打扰；纠缠
动词（旧义）：令人烦恼；使人不快

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「烦恼；恼人的事」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「感到恼火的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的」
由 annoying 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「恼人地」

senses.title: To make someone slightly angry
senses.definition: to cause mild anger or irritation, usually through repeated small actions
senses.definitionCN: 通常因反复的小动作而引起轻微恼怒或不耐烦
senses.example: The repeated rustling began to annoy everyone at the long table.
senses.exampleCN: 反复的窸窣声开始让长桌旁所有人都心烦。
senses.why: The French source meant to trouble and weary; annoyance is a wearing-down rather than a blow.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「使人烦扰、使厌倦」；annoy 是一种慢慢磨损，而不是一记重击。

senses.title: To pester or bother repeatedly
senses.definition: to keep disturbing someone with requests or unwanted attention
senses.definitionCN: 不断以请求或不必要的关注打扰某人
senses.example: The boy annoyed his sister until she gave him the book.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩一直缠着姐姐，直到她把书给了他。
senses.why: When the same small disturbance repeats, the irritation compounds and the verb takes on the idea of pestering.
senses.whyCN: 同一个小的干扰反复出现，烦躁就会叠加，动词于是带上「纠缠」的意思。

senses.title: To cause physical discomfort
senses.definition: in older use, to trouble or hurt a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指使身体某部位不适或疼痛
senses.example: The tight band annoyed the wound and had to be loosened.
senses.exampleCN: 绷带勒得伤口不适，只好把它放松。
senses.why: The original sense was broad trouble, so physical discomfort was included before the word narrowed to mild anger.
senses.whyCN: 最初的词义是广义的「烦扰」，因此在收窄为「轻微发怒」之前也包括身体上的不适。

senses.title: To feel irritated, in the passive
senses.definition: in the passive frames be annoyed at or be annoyed with, to feel irritated by something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动结构 be annoyed at 或 be annoyed with，表示因某事或某人而感到恼火
senses.example: She was annoyed with herself for forgetting the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为忘了会议而生自己的气。
senses.why: The passive puts the person on the receiving end: the disturbance acts, and the person is annoyed.
senses.whyCN: 被动结构让人处在承受的一端：干扰在施加，人是被烦到的一方。

intro.en: Annoy began as a Latin phrase about hatred, passed through French, and softened into mild irritation.
intro.cn: annoy 起初是一个关于「憎恨」的拉丁短语，经法语传入后逐渐软化为轻微的恼怒。

items.en: The phrase in odio meant 'in hatred', from odium 'hatred'. To have someone in hatred was to regard them with hostility.
items.cn: 短语 in odio 意为「在憎恨之中」，来自 odium「憎恨」。把某人「置于憎恨里」，就是以敌意对待他。

items.en: The verb enuier meant 'to trouble, to vex, to weary', carrying the Latin phrase into everyday emotional life.
items.cn: 动词 enuier 意为「使烦扰、使烦恼、使厌倦」，把那个拉丁短语带入日常情感生活。

items.en: The noun enui meant 'trouble, annoyance'; it later became English ennui, a deep boredom.
items.cn: 名词 enui 意为「烦扰、烦恼」，后来还变成英语的 ennui，指深层的倦怠无聊。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as annoy, first in the strong sense of harming or troubling. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语把动词借入为 annoy，起初是「伤害、烦扰」的强义；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense weakens to mild irritation, and the passive frames be annoyed at and be annoyed with become standard.
items.cn: 词义弱化为轻微的恼怒，被动搭配 be annoyed at 与 be annoyed with 成为标准用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the annoyance family plus its French cousin ennui; the near-meaning group ranks ways of disturbing someone.
note.cn: 形近组收 annoyance 词族及其法语表亲 ennui；近义组按打扰方式排列。

entries.definition: The feeling of being irritated, or the thing that causes it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烦恼」或「恼人的事」，指被惹恼的感受或引发这种感受的东西。

entries.definition: Adjective: feeling mild anger or irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感到恼火的」，指人处在轻微愤怒之中。

entries.definition: Adjective: causing irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人恼火的」，指某事物引起烦躁。

entries.definition: Deep boredom and listlessness, borrowed from French from the same Latin phrase in odio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倦怠、无聊」，借自法语，与 annoy 同出拉丁短语 in odio。

entries.definition: To make someone mildly angry, often through a physical or repeated trigger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激怒、使恼火」，常由身体刺激或反复的触发引起。

entries.definition: To disturb or trouble someone; broader and often gentler than annoy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰、烦扰」，范围更宽，语气常比 annoy 轻。

entries.definition: To annoy repeatedly with requests or questions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「纠缠、不断烦扰」，指以请求或问题反复打扰。

entries.definition: Informal: to annoy or bother someone with repeated demands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，口语义为「烦扰、找麻烦」，指以反复要求给人添麻烦。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin hatred phrase and the passive frames that now carry the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「憎恨」短语，以及今天承载这种感受的被动句式。

normal.en: In odio is in hatred: annoy started as putting someone in a hated place.
normal.cn: in odio 是「在憎恨中」：annoy 起初是把某人放进被憎恨的位置。

normal.en: Ennui is the same French noun at a deeper level: annoyance can grow into boredom.
normal.cn: ennui 是同一个法语名词的更深一层：恼火也能长成倦怠。

normal.en: Be annoyed at a thing, be annoyed with a person.
normal.cn: 对事用 be annoyed at，对人用 be annoyed with。

normal.en: Annoyance is the feeling; annoying is the thing that causes it.
normal.cn: annoyance 是感受，annoying 是引发感受的东西。

normal.en: The word weakened over centuries from trouble to mild irritation.
normal.cn: 这个词在几百年间从「烦扰」弱化成「轻微恼怒」。

abstract.en: Picture a small insect circling an ear, brushed away, returning again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小虫绕着耳朵飞，被赶走又一遍遍回来。

abstract.en: Picture a stone in a shoe that cannot be taken out until the end of a long walk.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里的一颗石子，整段长路都取不出来。

abstract.en: Picture a dripping tap at night, one drop at a time, wearing patience thin.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里滴水的水龙头，一滴接一滴，把耐心磨薄。

examples.en: The repeated rustling began to annoy everyone at the long table.
examples.cn: 反复的窸窣声开始让长桌旁所有人都心烦。

examples.en: The boy annoyed his sister until she gave him the book.
examples.cn: 男孩一直缠着姐姐，直到她把书给了他。

examples.en: She was annoyed with herself for forgetting the meeting.
examples.cn: 她因为忘了会议而生自己的气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额闹一」——额头上青筋一闹，心里就烦一分：使恼怒

root: 拉丁语短语 in odio「在憎恨之中」来自 odium「憎恨」，经古法语动词 enuier「使烦扰」进入英语为 annoy，最初是较强的「伤害、烦扰」义，现代弱化为轻微的恼怒。同源名词 enui 还演变为英语 ennui「倦怠」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses trace one small disturbance: mild anger, repeated pestering, old bodily discomfort, and the passive state of being irritated.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项沿着同一个小干扰展开：轻微恼怒、反复纠缠、旧时的身体不适，以及被动的恼火状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny disturbance returns again and again until patience wears thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小小的干扰一再回来，直到耐心被磨薄。

branches.en: THE IRRITATION LINE: repeated small actions produce mild anger.
branches.cn: 恼怒线：反复的小动作产生轻微愤怒。

branches.en: THE PESTERING LINE: the disturbance is deliberate and keeps coming.
branches.cn: 纠缠线：干扰是刻意的，而且不断到来。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: the older broad sense covered physical discomfort.
branches.cn: 身体线：较早的宽泛词义包括身体上的不适。

branches.en: THE PASSIVE LINE: the person is on the receiving end of the disturbance.
branches.cn: 被动线：人处在承受干扰的一端。

branches.en: THE SHARED LINE: deliberate pestering and passive irritation are two sides of one exchange.
branches.cn: 交互线：刻意纠缠与被动恼火是同一次互动的两面。

intro.en: Annoy is a French verb from a Latin hatred phrase; English adds the usual noun and participle endings.
intro.cn: annoy 是来自拉丁语「憎恨」短语的法语动词，英语再为它加上普通的名词与分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin odium and odiosus are recorded, and the French forms are documented; nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 odium 与 odiosus 都有记录，法语形式也有文献可查，这里没有重构形式。

items.example: It locates the person inside hatred.
It is the key word of the old phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个古老短语的关键词。

items.example: It is the root behind the French verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是法语动词背后的词根。
它后来变成英语的 ennui。

items.example: English took this verb as annoy.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个动词借入为 annoy。

items.example: The verb also has a passive life.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也常以被动形式出现。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「烦恼；恼人的事」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「感到恼火的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的」

definition_en: the act of paying money, a sum of money that is paid, or something given in return for what someone has done
core_image: 一只信封从一只手递到另一只手里，封口处写着金额
scene: 月底的办公室里，会计把一叠单据摊在桌上。 The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里是「付款、支付」（第 1 个义项：付钱这一行为）；句意为公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。图中可辨识物件：单据、计算器、贴着标签的信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 payment 去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的基础动词，义为「支付」
由 pay 加 -able 构成，指应付的、可支付的
由 pay 加 -er 构成，指付款的一方
由 pay 加 -ee 构成，指收款的一方

senses.title: The act of paying money
senses.definition: the act of giving money for goods, work or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为货物、劳动或服务把钱交出去这一行为
senses.example: The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns a verb into the name of its action, so payment names the handing over itself rather than the money.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成动作的名称，所以 payment 先指「把钱交出去」这件事，而不是那笔钱。

senses.title: An amount of money paid
senses.definition: a sum of money that is paid or that has to be paid
senses.definitionCN: 已经付出或按约定需要付出的一笔钱
senses.example: The first payment is due at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 第一期款项在月底到期。
senses.why: Once the action has a name, the thing produced by the action takes the same noun, which is why payments can be counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 动作有了名称之后，动作产生的东西也用同一个名词，所以一笔一笔的款项可以数出来。

senses.title: A return for what someone has done
senses.definition: something given or suffered as a return for what a person has done
senses.definitionCN: 因某人做过的事而得到或承受的回报
senses.example: That was payment for years of neglect.
senses.exampleCN: 那是对多年冷落的报应。
senses.why: If paying is giving back what is owed, then any return can be called payment, and the word stretches from wages to punishment.
senses.whyCN: 既然付款是归还所欠，那么任何回报都可以叫 payment，这个词便从报酬一路延伸到惩罚。

intro.en: Payment is the English noun built on pay, and both go back through French to a Latin word for peace.
intro.cn: payment 是在 pay 之上构成的英语名词，二者都经法语回溯到一个表示和平的拉丁词。

items.en: Pax meant peace, and settling a claim was understood as restoring quiet between two sides.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，结清一笔索求被理解为让双方之间恢复安静。

items.en: The verb pacare meant to quiet or satisfy someone, and in medieval use it covered satisfying a creditor with money.
items.cn: 动词 pacare 意为使某人平静或满足，在中世纪的用法里包括用钱让债主满足。

items.en: Old French formed paiement from payer, adding its own noun ending to the verb for paying.
items.cn: 古法语由 payer 造出 paiement，给表示支付的动词加上自己的名词词尾。

items.en: Anglo-French carried the word into English legal and commercial writing, where fixed sums and dates mattered.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语把这个词带进英语的法律与商业文书，那里讲究固定的金额与日期。

items.en: Modern English keeps payment for the act, for each sum, and for a return of any kind, while pay names the wages themselves.
items.cn: 现代英语用 payment 指行为、每一笔金额以及任何形式的回报，而 pay 指工钱本身。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base verb, the two person forms and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for sums paid and for closing an account.
note.cn: 形近组收基础动词、两个指人的形式，以及一个只是外形相似的词；近义组收表示所付金额与结清账目的词。

entries.definition: The verb that payment is built on, meaning to give money for something.
entries.definitionCN: payment 所依附的动词，意为为某物付钱。

entries.definition: That must be paid, or able to be paid.
The person who receives a payment.
The hard surface beside a road, from a Latin verb meaning to beat down; only the ending looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 路旁的硬质路面，来自一个意为「夯平」的拉丁动词；只是词尾相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Money paid for a service or for a right.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项服务或某项权利付出的钱。

entries.definition: One of several fixed sums paid over a period.
entries.definitionCN: 分几期付出的一笔固定金额。

entries.definition: Money sent to someone, especially by post or transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 汇给某人的钱，尤指通过邮寄或转账。

entries.definition: The act of paying what is owed and ending a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 付清欠款并了结索求的行为。

normalIntro.en: The word is a verb plus a noun ending, and behind the verb sits a Latin idea of peace; the whole family is about making a claim go quiet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是动词加名词词尾，动词背后是拉丁语中「和平」的观念；整族词都在说让一项索求安静下来。

normal.en: Payment is pay plus -ment, the ending that turns an action into a noun, as in movement and argument.
normal.cn: payment 是 pay 加 -ment，这个后缀把动作变成名词，就像 movement 与 argument。

normal.en: Old French had paiement, so English did not invent the noun; it borrowed a ready-made form.
normal.cn: 古法语已有 paiement，英语并没有自造这个名词，而是借了一个现成的形式。

normal.en: Make a payment is the everyday phrase, because the noun names the act rather than a thing you can hold.
normal.cn: make a payment 是日常说法，因为这个名词指行为，而不是手里能拿住的东西。

normal.en: A down payment is the sum handed over first, before the rest follows in instalments.
normal.cn: down payment 是先交出的那一笔，其余部分随后分期付清。

normal.en: With payment the focus is on the act or the sum; with pay it is on the wages as a whole.
normal.cn: 用 payment 时焦点在行为或某一笔钱；用 pay 时焦点在作为整体的工钱。

abstract.en: Adding -ment to a verb is a way of freezing an action into something a contract can name.
abstract.cn: 给动词加 -ment，是把一个动作冻成合同可以指名的那样东西。

abstract.en: A payment is a promise made visible: the moment an obligation turns into something countable.
abstract.cn: 一笔付款是让承诺变得可见的时刻：义务变成了可以计数的东西。

abstract.en: The word keeps the old idea that money quiets a claim, which is why even a punishment can be called its payment.
abstract.cn: 这个词保留了「钱让索求安静」的旧观念，所以连惩罚也可以被称为它的报应。

examples.en: The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
examples.cn: 公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。

examples.en: The first payment is due at the end of the month.
examples.cn: 第一期款项在月底到期。

examples.en: They accept payment by card or by bank transfer.
examples.cn: 他们接受刷卡或银行转账付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赔门特」——像「赔」加上一道门，钱从门里递出去；payment 就是付出去的款。

root: pay（支付）加名词后缀 -ment 构成；pay 源自拉丁语 pax（和平）与 pacare（使平静、清偿），经古法语 payer 与 paiement 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of handing money over; from that act come the single sum paid and the wider idea of any return, good or bad.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把钱交出去这个动作；由它分出所付的一笔金额，以及任何回报（无论好坏）这一更宽的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed envelope passing from one hand to another, an amount written across the flap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只封好的信封从一只手递到另一只手里，封口上写着金额。

branches.en: a transfer completed before a deadline
branches.cn: 在截止前完成的一笔转账

branches.en: a numbered first sum due at month end
branches.cn: 月底到期、编号为第一期的一笔钱

branches.en: an old neglect finally answered
branches.cn: 多年的冷落终于得到回应

branches.en: the act and the sum share one noun
branches.cn: 行为与金额共用一个名词

branches.en: what is counted and what is returned
branches.cn: 被计数的那笔与被归还的那份

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted verb with an English noun ending, and the Latin root itself began as a word for peace.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根的动词加上英语名词词尾，而那个拉丁词根本身最初表示和平。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: to start an organization or system, or to prove something is true
core_image: 打下第一根桩，让一座建筑稳稳立在地上
scene: 这所大学建立于一百多年前，最初只有两个系。 The university was established over a hundred years ago with only two departments.
sceneCN: 这里 establish 是「建立」（第 1 个义项：创办机构或制度）；句意：这所大学建立于一百多年前，最初只有两个系。

senses.title: Set up an organization
senses.definition: to start a company, school or system that will continue
senses.definitionCN: 创办一个将持续运作的公司、学校或制度
senses.example: They established a school in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在村里创办了一所学校。
senses.why: The Latin source means to make stable, so establishing puts something on a firm base.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为使稳固，因此 establish 就是把事物放在坚实的基础上。

senses.title: Make accepted or secure
senses.definition: to make something accepted, respected or secure
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物被接受、受尊重或稳固下来
senses.example: The team established a strong lead.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍确立了明显的领先优势。
senses.why: What stands firm is secure, so establishing also means settling something firmly.
senses.whyCN: 站得稳就是稳固，因此 establish 也指把事物牢牢确定下来。

senses.title: Prove or find out
senses.definition: to discover or prove facts with evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用证据发现或证明事实
senses.example: Police are trying to establish the cause of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正努力查明火灾原因。
senses.why: A fact placed on firm evidence is established beyond doubt.
senses.whyCN: 建立在坚实证据上的事实，就被毫无疑问地确立了。

intro.en: Establish comes from Old French establir, from Latin stabilire, to make stable.
intro.cn: establish 源自古法语 establir，源自拉丁语 stabilire（使稳固）。

items.en: Stare means to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Stabilire means to make stable.
items.cn: stabilire 意为使稳固。

items.en: Establir means to set up firmly.
items.cn: establir 意为牢固地设立。

items.en: Establish covers founding and proving.
items.cn: establish 兼指创立与证实。

items.en: Established also describes long-accepted things.
items.cn: established 也描述长期被接受的事物。

note.en: Establish is close to found and set up, and shares a root with stable.
note.cn: establish 与创立、设立相近，并与 stable 同根。

entries.definition: the act of setting up
long accepted
to set up again
to start an organization
to arrange or begin something
to show that something is true

normalIntro.en: Establish is about a stable table: once its legs are firm, it stands.
normalIntro.cn: establish 就像一张稳固的桌子：腿站稳了，它就立住了。

normal.en: Establish a company means bring a new business into being.
normal.cn: establish a company 意为让新企业诞生。

normal.en: Establish contact means make a connection.
normal.cn: establish contact 意为建立联系。

normal.en: Establish the facts means find out what really happened.
normal.cn: establish the facts 意为查明真实情况。

normal.en: A well established habit is hard to break.
normal.cn: well established 的习惯很难改掉。

normal.en: Compare found: found starts an institution, establish also makes it secure.
normal.cn: 对比 found：found 侧重创办，establish 还强调使其稳固。

abstract.en: Picture a cornerstone laid before any wall rises.
abstract.cn: 想象墙还没砌起就先放好的基石。

abstract.en: Imagine roots spreading deep under a young tree.
abstract.cn: 想象树根在幼树下方深深蔓延。

abstract.en: Think of a flag planted firmly on a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象旗帜牢牢插在山顶。

examples.en: The charity was established in 1990.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构成立于一九九零年。

examples.en: She quickly established herself as a leader.
examples.cn: 她很快确立了自己作为领导者的地位。

examples.en: Experts have not yet established the cause.
examples.cn: 专家尚未查明原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ stable（稳固的）＋ ish」——让事物稳稳立出来，就是建立；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站）→ stabilire（使稳固）→ 古法语 establir → establish，核心义「让事物稳稳站住、扎下根」。

sensesIntro.en: Establish first means found an organization, then make something secure, and finally prove a fact.
sensesIntro.cn: establish 先指创办机构，再指使某事物稳固，最后指证实事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first post driven deep so a building can stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一根桩深深打入，让建筑得以立起。

branches.en: Founding gives an organization its start.
branches.cn: 创办给机构一个开始。

branches.en: Making something secure gives it a firm place.
branches.cn: 使事物稳固，就是给它一个坚实的位置。

branches.en: Facts established by evidence stand firm.
branches.cn: 由证据确立的事实站得住脚。

branches.en: A new institution must become established to last.
branches.cn: 新机构必须站稳才能长久。

branches.en: A proven claim is an established claim.
branches.cn: 被证明的论断就是已确立的论断。

intro.en: Establish is built on Latin stabilis, steady, and the verb ending -ish.
intro.cn: establish 建立在拉丁语 stabilis（稳固的）与动词词尾 -ish 之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilire means to make stable, from stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stabilire 意为使稳固，来自 stare（站立）。

items.example: Stare gives the idea of standing.
Stabilis means able to stand firm.
Old French establir carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 establir 传递了该词。

definition_zh: 强大的；有权势的；有影响力的；有力的；效力大的；感染力强的
definition_en: having great power, strength or influence, or able to produce a strong effect on people or things
core_image: 大坝深处一台水轮机被急流推动，钢铁外壳微微震动
scene: 山口的旧风车被换成了新的发电机，叶片在大风里转得飞快。 The new turbine is powerful enough to light the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 powerful 是「强大的、力量大的」（第 2 个义项：物理力量强）；句意为新水轮机的力量足以照亮整个村子。图中可辨识物件：山口、发电机、大风、叶片。

pos.zh: 强大的；有权势的；有力的；效力大的；感染力强的

derivatives.zh: 由 powerful 加 -ly 构成，义为「强有力地；强烈地」
由 powerful 加 -ness 构成，义为「强大；有力」
由 power 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无力的；无权势的」
由 power 与 house 复合，义为「发电厂；精力充沛的人或机构」

senses.title: Having great power or influence
senses.definition: having a lot of control over people, events or decisions
senses.definitionCN: 对他人、事件或决定拥有很大的控制力
senses.example: The mayor is the most powerful figure in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 市长是这座城市里最有权势的人物。
senses.why: Power is the ability to make things happen, and -ful says a person is full of it; the first sense is power over other people.
senses.whyCN: power 是让事情发生的能力，-ful 表示「充满」，所以第一个义项是对他人的支配力。

senses.title: Physically strong or forceful
senses.definition: having great physical strength or able to produce a lot of force
senses.definitionCN: 具有很大的物理力量，或能产生很大的力
senses.example: The old truck has a surprisingly powerful engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧卡车的发动机力量大得惊人。
senses.why: The same fullness applies to machines and bodies, where power can be measured in force, speed or output rather than in votes.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「充满」也用在机器与身体上，那里的力量可以用力、速度或输出来衡量，而不是用选票。

senses.title: Producing a strong effect
senses.definition: having a strong effect on the body, on a situation or on a result
senses.definitionCN: 对身体、局势或结果产生强烈作用
senses.example: Doctors gave him a powerful drug for the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给他用了一种强效止痛药。
senses.why: If something acts with force on a body or on events, it is powerful in effect, so the word reaches medicine and argument as well as politics.
senses.whyCN: 某物若对身体或事态施加强力，就是在效果上强大，于是这个词也走进医药与论辩，不只属于政治。

senses.title: Moving or impressive
senses.titleCN: 感染力强的；令人震撼的
senses.definition: producing a strong emotional impression on an audience
senses.definitionCN: 在观众心里留下强烈的情感印象
senses.example: Her speech was powerful enough to silence the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演讲感染力极强，整个礼堂都安静下来。
senses.why: An effect on feelings is still an effect; once the word measures impact, a film or a sentence can be powerful without any physical force.
senses.whyCN: 对情感的作用也是一种作用；一旦这个词开始衡量冲击力，一部电影或一句话即使没有物理力量也能是 powerful。

senses.title: Loud and far-reaching in sound
senses.definition: of a voice or sound, strong enough to be heard at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 指嗓音或声音，响到远处也能听见
senses.example: The actor's powerful voice reached the last row without a microphone.
senses.exampleCN: 演员洪亮的嗓音不用麦克风也传到了最后一排。
senses.why: Sound that acts strongly on the ear is effect in the air, so the adjective reaches the voice.
senses.whyCN: 对耳朵作用强烈的声音就是空气中的效果，形容词便延伸到嗓音上。

senses.title: Rich and concentrated in taste or smell
senses.definition: of a taste, smell or wine, strong and concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 指味道、气味或酒，浓烈而醇厚
senses.example: The cheese has a powerful smell that fills the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这奶酪气味浓烈，满屋子都是。
senses.why: A strong effect on the senses is the same fullness of force, so flavour takes the word too.
senses.whyCN: 对感官的强烈作用仍是同一种「力满」，味道也就用上了这个词。

senses.title: Built with great strength of structure
senses.titleCN: 结实的；构造坚固有力的
senses.definition: of a body, machine or structure, built to withstand great force
senses.definitionCN: 指身体、机器或结构，造得能承受巨大的力
senses.example: The bridge has powerful steel supports.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥有坚固有力的钢支架。
senses.why: What is full of power must hold together under force, so the word reaches the parts that resist it.
senses.whyCN: 充满力量的东西必须在力的作用下不散架，于是这个词也指承受力的部件。

senses.title: Great in amount or degree
senses.titleCN: 程度极大的；力度很强的
senses.definition: of a movement or blow, done with great force or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 指动作或打击，用出很大的力道或强度
senses.example: The swimmer made a powerful kick and shot ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳运动员猛力一蹬腿，冲到了前面。
senses.why: An action full of power is one whose whole body goes into it, which extends the adjective to motion.
senses.whyCN: 充满力量的动作就是全身投入的动作，形容词由此延伸到动作本身。

intro.en: Powerful is the noun power plus -ful, full of; power itself comes from Latin posse, to be able, through Old French.
intro.cn: powerful 是名词 power 加 -ful（充满）；power 本身经古法语上溯拉丁语 posse（能够）。

items.en: Posse meant to be able or to have the strength to do something, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: posse 意为能够、有力量做某事，是这一族词共同的根。

items.en: Everyday Latin used potere for can or be able, and this form spread through the provinces.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语用 potere 表示「能、可以」，这个形式在各省广泛流传。

items.en: Old French turned it into the noun poeir, meaning ability, strength or authority.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成名词 poeir，意为能力、力量或权威。

items.en: English borrowed power in the Middle Ages and added -ful to build an adjective meaning full of power.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入 power，并加上 -ful 造出表示「充满力量」的形容词。

items.en: Modern English applies powerful to people, states, engines, drugs, arguments and speeches, keeping one core of force.
items.cn: 现代英语把 powerful 用在人物、国家、发动机、药物、论据与演讲上，核心始终是「力量」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same power family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for strength and influence.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 power 词族的形式；近义组收表示力量与影响力的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective, naming ability, strength or control.
entries.definitionCN: 这一形容词背后的名词，指能力、力量或支配力。

entries.definition: In a powerful way, with great force or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 由 powerful 加 -ly 构成，义为「强有力地」。

entries.definition: Without power or the ability to act.
entries.definitionCN: 由 power 加 -less 构成，义为「无力的；无能为力的」。

entries.definition: A power station, or a person or group full of energy and strength.
entries.definitionCN: 由 power 与 house 复合，指发电厂，也指精力充沛的人或机构。

entries.definition: Having great physical strength, often in the body or in a material.
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的；多指身体或材料本身的强度。

entries.definition: Very strong or great, a word with an old and slightly literary ring.
entries.definitionCN: 强大的；气势宏大的，带古老且偏文学的色彩。

entries.definition: Full of force in expression or action, often said of people and words.
entries.definitionCN: 有力的；多形容表达或行动，常指人与言辞。

entries.definition: Able to change decisions or opinions indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 有影响力的；强调间接改变决定或看法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a noun of ability with a suffix meaning full of, and its family keeps returning to force, control and effect.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示能力的名词加上「充满」的后缀，同族词反复回到力量、支配与效果。

normal.en: Power comes from Latin posse, to be able, through Old French poeir.
normal.cn: power 来自拉丁语 posse（能够），经古法语 poeir 传入。

normal.en: -ful means full of, so powerful is simply full of power, with no other root involved.
normal.cn: -ful 意为「充满」，所以 powerful 就是「充满力量」，没有别的词根。

normal.en: Powerless swaps -ful for -less and turns the meaning around.
normal.cn: powerless 把 -ful 换成 -less，意思就反了过来。

normal.en: A powerful engine and a powerful argument share one idea: both move something with force.
normal.cn: 力量大的发动机与有力的论据共用一个想法：都以力推动某物。

normal.en: Powerfully adds -ly and describes how that force is applied.
normal.cn: powerfully 加 -ly，描述这股力量是怎样施加的。

abstract.en: Power is the ability to make something happen, and powerful measures how much of that ability a thing holds.
abstract.cn: 力量是让事情发生的能力，powerful 衡量的就是某物握有多少这种能力。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a person to a machine because both can push the world in a chosen direction.
abstract.cn: 这个词能轻易从人转到机器，因为两者都能把世界推向某个选定的方向。

abstract.en: A powerful speech leaves the room different, which shows that force is not only physical.
abstract.cn: 一场感染力强的演讲会让房间变得不同，可见力量并不只属于身体。

examples.en: The new turbine is powerful enough to light the whole village.
examples.cn: 新水轮机的力量足以照亮整个村子。

examples.en: The mayor is the most powerful figure in the city.
examples.cn: 市长是这座城市里最有权势的人物。

examples.en: Doctors gave him a powerful drug for the pain.
examples.cn: 医生给他用了一种强效止痛药。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「炮火」——炮火一响，声势逼人；powerful 就是强大的、有力的。

root: 由名词 power 加形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成；power 经古法语 poeir 上溯通俗拉丁语 potere 与拉丁语 posse（能够），与 potent、potential 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being full of power; the senses divide into social influence, physical force, strong effect and emotional impact.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「充满力量」；义项由此分出社会权势、物理力量、强烈效力与情感冲击。

branches.cn: 市长走向一排麦克风

branches.en: a turbine turning under rushing water
branches.cn: 水轮机在水流下转动

branches.en: a small vial of a drug that stops the pain
branches.cn: 一小瓶止住疼痛的药

branches.en: a hall going silent after one sentence
branches.cn: 一句话之后整个礼堂安静下来

branches.en: a machine strong enough to lift a loaded truck
branches.cn: 一台力量足以吊起满载卡车的机器

intro.en: The adjective is the noun power plus a suffix meaning full of, and the noun itself goes back to a Latin verb for being able.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是名词 power 加上表示「充满」的后缀，而名词本身上溯一个意为「能够」的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Powerful rests on Latin posse, to be able, and its everyday form potere, which Old French turned into the noun poeir; potent and potential share the same root.
latinIntro.cn: powerful 立足于拉丁语 posse（能够）及其日常形式 potere，古法语由此造出名词 poeir；potent 与 potential 同出一根。

senses.title: Cook in hot oil
senses.definition: to cook food in a small amount of hot oil
senses.definitionCN: 用少量热油烹调食物
senses.example: She fried an egg in hot oil.
senses.exampleCN: 她在热油里煎了一个鸡蛋。
senses.why: This is the basic kitchen sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的厨房义项。

senses.title: Toss in a hot pan
senses.definition: to cook small pieces of food quickly in hot oil while moving them
senses.definitionCN: 在热油中快速翻动小块食物
senses.example: He fried the rice with vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 他把米饭和蔬菜一起炒。
senses.why: Stir-frying is a fast, moving kind of frying.
senses.whyCN: 快炒是一种快速、不断翻动的煎炒。

senses.title: The potato sticks
senses.definition: thin pieces of potato cooked in hot oil, usually called fries
senses.definitionCN: 在热油中炸成的细条土豆，通常用复数 fries
senses.example: We ordered burgers and fries.
senses.exampleCN: 我们点了汉堡和炸薯条。

items.en: The spelling settled as fry.

items.en: The plural fries named potato sticks.
items.cn: 复数 fries 用来指炸薯条。

note.en: Fry is compared with look-alike words and other cooking verbs.

definition_zh: 实际的；实践的；实用的；可行的；注重实际的；务实的
definition_en: relating to real actions and situations rather than ideas, useful for a real purpose, likely to work, or sensible about everyday needs
core_image: 一张折起的图纸被塞进工具袋，袋口露出半截卷尺
scene: 教室后面的工作台上，几个学生把图纸放下，开始用木条搭架子。 The course gives students practical experience with real tools.
sceneCN: 这里 practical 是「实际的、实践的」（第 1 个义项：与真实行动有关，而非只讲理论）；句意为这门课让学生在真实工具上获得实际经验。图中可辨识物件：工作台、图纸、木条、工具袋。

pos.zh: 实际的；实践的；实用的；可行的；注重实际的；务实的

collocations.zh: 实际上；就实际效果而言

derivatives.zh: 由 practical 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；几乎」
由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」
由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的；不可行的」

senses.title: Concerned with action rather than theory
senses.definition: connected with real actions and situations rather than with ideas or rules alone
senses.definitionCN: 与真实行动和情形相连，而不只是与观念或规则相连
senses.example: Students need practical experience before they apply for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在申请这份工作之前需要有实际经验。
senses.why: Greek praktikos meant fit for action, so the adjective begins by pointing at doing rather than at thinking; the first sense keeps that contrast alive.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 praktikos 意为「适合行动的」，所以这个形容词从一开始就指向做而不是想；第一个义项保留的正是这组对照。

senses.title: Useful for a real purpose
senses.definition: designed to be useful in real use rather than attractive or clever
senses.definitionCN: 为真实使用而设计得有用，而不是为了好看或机巧
senses.example: The kit contains a practical set of tools for small repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这套工具里是一组做小修小补很实用的工具。
senses.why: If a thing suits action, it is useful, and the word passes from the situation to the object that fits it.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西若适合行动，就是有用的；词义于是从情形转到适合这个情形的物件上。

senses.title: Likely to work
senses.definition: possible to carry out and likely to succeed in real conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下做得到、并且很可能成功
senses.example: Building a footbridge here is the most practical solution.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里修一座人行桥是最可行的办法。
senses.why: A plan is practical when it survives real conditions, so the adjective shifts from describing tools to judging proposals.
senses.whyCN: 一个方案能在真实条件下站住，就是可行的；形容词于是从评价器物转向评判方案。

senses.title: Sensible about everyday needs
senses.definition: of a person, dealing with things as they are and not chasing impractical ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指人按事物的实际情况办事，不追求不切实际的想法
senses.example: She is practical about money and never buys on impulse.
senses.exampleCN: 她花钱很务实，从不冲动购物。
senses.why: A person whose habits suit action is called practical, which is how the word reaches character and not just objects.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的习惯若总适合行动，就会被称作务实；这个词由此触及性格，而不只是器物。

senses.title: Virtual, existing in effect
senses.definition: existing in fact or effect although not officially so
senses.definitionCN: 虽非正式如此，但在事实或效果上确实如此
senses.example: He is the practical leader of the team, though no one gave him the title.
senses.exampleCN: 他其实是团队事实上的领队，尽管没人给他这个头衔。
senses.why: What works in real action is what is real, so the word names de facto standing.
senses.whyCN: 在真实行动中管用的才是真的，这个词便指事实上的地位。

senses.title: Learnable by doing
senses.definition: of knowledge or skills, gained by doing things rather than by study alone
senses.definitionCN: 指知识或技能，靠动手而非单靠书本获得
senses.example: Driving is a practical skill you cannot learn from a book.
senses.exampleCN: 开车是动手的技能，光看书学不会。
senses.why: Action teaches what theory cannot, so the adjective reaches the kind of learning itself.
senses.whyCN: 行动能教书本教不了的东西，形容词便延伸到学习方式上。

senses.title: Suitable for a particular real use
senses.definition: suited to a particular real purpose or occasion
senses.definitionCN: 适合某个真实的用途或场合
senses.example: Wear practical shoes for the hike.
senses.exampleCN: 远足要穿合适的鞋。
senses.why: A thing that fits the action it serves is practical, so the word reaches design and choice.
senses.whyCN: 能配合它所服务之事的物件就是实用的，这个词便延伸到设计与选择上。

senses.title: A practical: a lesson in doing
senses.definition: an examination or lesson in which skills are demonstrated by doing, not by writing
senses.definitionCN: 以动手演示而非笔试来考查技能的课程或考试
senses.example: She passed her chemistry practical on the first try.
senses.exampleCN: 她一次就通过了化学实操考试。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the lesson where action itself is the test.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词，指那种以行动本身为考核的课。

intro.en: Practical follows an action word from Greek through Latin and French: praktikos, practicus, pratique, and finally the English adjective built on practice.
intro.cn: practical 沿着一个表示行动的词从希腊语经拉丁语与法语走来：praktikos、practicus、pratique，最后是英语在 practice 上造出的形容词。

items.en: The Greek verb prassein meant to do, to act or to carry something through.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 prassein 意为做、行动或把事情办成。

items.en: Praktikos was formed from it to mean fit for action, practical rather than theoretical.
items.cn: 由它构成的 praktikos 意为「适合行动的」，指务实的而非理论的。

items.en: Latin took the adjective as practicus, used for what concerns action or practice.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借作 practicus，用于表示与行动或实践有关的事物。

items.en: English borrowed practice through Old French, first for the doing of something and then for repeated exercise.
items.cn: 英语经古法语借入 practice，先指做某件事，后指反复练习。

items.en: Modern English built practical on practice with -al, and the word spread to tools, plans, people and purposes.
items.cn: 现代英语在 practice 上加 -al 造出 practical，这个词随后扩展到工具、方案、人与目的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same practice family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what works in real conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 practice 词族的形式；近义组收形容在真实条件下行得通的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for doing something repeatedly or for the usual way of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，指反复练习，或通常的做法。

entries.definition: In a practical way, and in everyday use also almost.
entries.definitionCN: 由 practical 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上」，日常也指「几乎」。

entries.definition: The quality of being useful or workable.
entries.definitionCN: 由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」。

entries.definition: Not sensible or not possible to carry out.
entries.definitionCN: 由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的」。

entries.definition: Dealing with things according to what works rather than what is ideal.
entries.definitionCN: 务实的；按是否行得通而非是否理想来处理事情。

entries.definition: Accepting the facts of a situation and not expecting too much.
entries.definitionCN: 现实的；接受实际情况，不抱过高期望。

entries.definition: Able to help you do something or get what you want.
entries.definitionCN: 有用的；能帮人做成事或得到想要的东西。

entries.definition: Able to be used or carried out successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 可行的；能够实施并取得效果的。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Greek verb for doing, and its family keeps returning to action, use and what actually works.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自希腊语表示「做」的动词，同族词反复回到行动、用途以及真正行得通的东西。

normal.en: Practical goes back through Latin practicus to Greek praktikos, fit for action.
normal.cn: practical 经拉丁语 practicus 上溯希腊语 praktikos（适合行动的）。

normal.en: The Greek verb prassein means to do, so the word is about doing rather than about thinking.
normal.cn: 希腊语动词 prassein 意为做，所以这个词讲的是做，而不是想。

normal.en: Practice is the noun for doing something repeatedly, and practical describes what suits that doing.
normal.cn: practice 是表示反复做某事的名词，practical 则形容适合这种做的东西。

normal.en: Impractical adds im- and names what cannot be carried out in real conditions.
normal.cn: impractical 加 im-，指在真实条件下办不成的事。

normal.en: Practically is the adverb of the same family, and it also picked up the everyday sense of almost.
normal.cn: practically 是同族的副词，还另外长出了「几乎」这个日常义。

abstract.en: A practical idea is one that survives contact with a real room, a real budget and a real deadline.
abstract.cn: 一个实用的想法，是能挺过真实房间、真实预算与真实期限的想法。

abstract.en: Theory describes what should happen; the practical answer is what still works when it does not.
abstract.cn: 理论描述本该发生什么；可行的答案则在事情没按预期发生时仍然管用。

abstract.en: Calling a person practical is a quiet compliment: it means the world rarely surprises them.
abstract.cn: 说一个人务实是含蓄的称赞：意思是世界很少让他措手不及。

examples.en: The course gives students practical experience with real tools.
examples.cn: 这门课让学生用真实工具获得实际经验。

examples.en: Building a footbridge here is the most practical solution.
examples.cn: 在这里修一座人行桥是最可行的办法。

examples.en: She is practical about money and never buys on impulse.
examples.cn: 她花钱很务实，从不冲动购物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来克」——伸手就能扑到、拿起来就能用的东西，才叫 practical（实用的、可行的）。

root: 源自希腊语 praktikos（适合行动的），出自动词 prassein（做、行动），经拉丁语 practicus 与古法语 pratique 进入英语；英语在 practice 的基础上加 -al 造出形容词 practical。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what suits action; the senses divide into real experience, usefulness, workability and a sensible temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「适合行动」；义项由此分出真实经验、实用、可行性，以及务实的性情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded drawing pushed into a tool bag, a tape measure sticking out of the pocket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折起的图纸被塞进工具袋，袋口露出半截卷尺。

branches.en: a student tightening a screw on a wooden frame
branches.cn: 学生把螺丝拧紧在木架上

branches.en: a small tool kit laid out on a table
branches.cn: 桌上摊开的一小套工具

branches.en: a footbridge drawn across a narrow stream
branches.cn: 横跨小溪的人行桥设计

branches.en: a shopper putting an item back on the shelf
branches.cn: 顾客把商品放回货架

branches.en: a repair done with what the room already holds
branches.cn: 用屋里现成的东西完成的修理

intro.en: Greek action words passed through Latin and French, and English built the adjective on practice with the suffix -al.
intro.cn: 表示行动的希腊词经拉丁语与法语传来，英语又在 practice 上加 -al 造出这个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Practical reaches back to Greek praxis and praktikos, which Latin took as practicus; the English adjective itself was formed later on practice.
latinIntro.cn: practical 上溯希腊语 praxis 与 praktikos，拉丁语借作 practicus；英语形容词本身则是后来在 practice 上造出的。

definition_zh: 正义；公正；公平；司法；审判；法官（头衔）
definition_en: the quality of being fair and right, or the system that courts use to decide what is right
core_image: 蒙眼的女像一手持天平，一手持剑，稳稳立在台阶之上
scene: 法院门口的台阶上，两排石柱之间刻着一句关于公平的铭文。 The family is still waiting for justice after ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 justice 是「公正、正义」（第 1 个义项：公平正当的品质），句意为十年过去，这家人仍在等待公正。画面里的物件：法院、台阶、石刻铭文。

pos.zh: 名词：正义；公正；司法；审判；（法官头衔）大法官

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「公正的」
由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」
同源动词，义为「证明正当」
加前缀 in- 构成，义为「不公正」
由 justice 派生，指司法官或司法机构

senses.title: Fairness as a quality
senses.definition: the quality of being fair and giving each person what is due
senses.definitionCN: 公平待人、各得其所的品质
senses.example: She fought for justice for the workers.
senses.exampleCN: 她为工人们争取公正。
senses.why: The core is fairness treated as a thing worth having and defending.
senses.whyCN: 核心是被当作值得争取与守护之物的公平。

senses.title: The system of courts
senses.definition: the legal system and the process of judging cases
senses.definitionCN: 法律体系以及审理案件的程序
senses.example: The case will go through the criminal justice system.
senses.exampleCN: 此案将走刑事司法程序。
senses.why: Fairness put into institutions becomes a system of courts and procedure.
senses.whyCN: 公平被装进机构，就变成法院与程序构成的体系。

senses.title: A fair outcome for someone
senses.definition: the fair result that a person has been denied or is owed
senses.definitionCN: 被剥夺或应得的那份公平结果
senses.example: The families finally got justice in court.
senses.exampleCN: 这些家庭终于在法庭上得到了公正。
senses.why: Here the abstract quality turns into a concrete settlement someone receives.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象的品质变成某人实际得到的结果。

senses.title: A title for a judge
senses.definition: a formal title for a judge of a high court
senses.definitionCN: 高等法院法官的正式头衔
senses.example: Justice Hill wrote the opinion for the court.
senses.exampleCN: 希尔大法官为法庭撰写了意见。
senses.why: A person who embodies fairness in court takes the abstract noun as a title.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上代表公平的人，直接拿了那个抽象名词当头衔。

senses.title: Fair treatment in presentation
senses.definition: the quality of doing full justice to a subject or a person
senses.definitionCN: 指充分、恰当呈现某题材或某人的水准
senses.example: The film does justice to a difficult story.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影充分展现了那个难讲的故事。
senses.why: Giving a subject its due is the same fairness applied to description.
senses.whyCN: 把题材应得的分量给它，是公平用在了描写上。

senses.title: Rightness in judgement
senses.definition: the correctness of a decision or evaluation
senses.definitionCN: 指决定或评价的正确恰当
senses.example: There is some justice in his complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他的抱怨有几分道理。
senses.why: A verdict that measures correctly is justice in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 量得准确的一次判断，就是缩小的正义。

intro.en: Justice comes from Latin justitia, fairness, from justus, lawful, and jus, law, through Old French.
intro.cn: justice 来自拉丁语 justitia「公平」，源自 justus「合法的」与 jus「法」，经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: justitia named the quality of being just, and justus came from jus, law.
items.cn: justitia 指「公正的品质」，justus 源自 jus「法」。

items.en: Old French justise carried both fairness and the right to judge.
items.cn: 古法语 justise 同时带着公平与审判权两层意思。

items.en: English took justice in the twelfth century for fairness and the courts.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪借入 justice，指公平与法庭。

items.en: The title Justice for a high court judge settled in later use.
items.cn: 作为高院法官头衔的 Justice 在后世固定下来。

items.en: The phrase do justice to extended it to art and description.
items.cn: do justice to 这一说法把它延伸到艺术与描写。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin law root; the near-meaning group holds other words for fairness and law.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁「法」词根；近义组收其他表示公平与法律的词。

entries.definition: Fair, or exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，义为「公正的」或「正好」。

entries.definition: To give good reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「证明正当」。

entries.definition: Unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 加 in- 构成，义为「不公正」。

entries.definition: The quality of treating people equally.
entries.definitionCN: 最日常的「公平」，语气朴素。

entries.definition: Fairness, especially where equal treatment must be adjusted.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指衡平与实质公平。

entries.definition: The set of rules a society enforces.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会强制执行的法律规则本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from Latin jus to the steps of a courthouse.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语 jus「法」走到法院门前的台阶。

normal.en: The root jus, law, also gives just and justify.
normal.cn: 词根 jus「法」还生出 just 与 justify。

normal.en: Bring someone to justice means get them into court.
normal.cn: bring someone to justice 指把人送上法庭。

normal.en: Do justice to is about showing something fully.
normal.cn: do justice to 指把某物充分表现出来。

normal.en: Justice can mean both the quality and the courts.
normal.cn: justice 既指公正的品质，也指司法机关。

normal.en: Injustice is simply justice with in-.
normal.cn: injustice 就是 justice 加 in-。

abstract.en: Justice is a scale held steady by an unseen hand.
abstract.cn: 正义是一杆被看不见的手扶稳的秤。

abstract.en: The same word is a principle and a building.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既是原则也是一座建筑。

abstract.en: It is fairness given an address and a date.
abstract.cn: 它就是有了地址和日期的公平。

examples.en: They demanded justice for the victims.
examples.cn: 他们为受害者要求公正。

examples.en: The justice system is slow but open.
examples.cn: 司法体系运转缓慢但公开。

examples.en: No photograph can do justice to that valley.
examples.cn: 任何照片都无法展现那条山谷的全部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎斯蒂斯」—— 秤杆扎稳了，才有正义

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」→ justus「合法的」→ justitia「公正」→ 古法语 justise → 英语 justice；同族 just、justify、injustice。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: fairness as a quality, the court system, a fair outcome, a judge's title, full presentation, and the rightness of a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：公正的品质、司法体系、应得的公正结果、大法官头衔、充分展现，以及评判得当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blindfolded figure holding scales and a sword.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒙眼持秤与剑的女像。

branches.en: THE BANNER: a principle that people march for.
branches.cn: 旗帜这条线：人们为之游行的一条原则。

branches.en: THE COURTHOUSE: procedure, lawyers, and hours of waiting.
branches.cn: 法院这条线：程序、律师和漫长的等待。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: a fair result handed to a family.
branches.cn: 裁决这条线：交到家属手里的公正结果。

branches.en: THE BENCH: a title spoken with a name.
branches.cn: 法官席这条线：念出姓氏的头衔。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: a work that shows its subject fully and fairly.
branches.cn: 作品这条线：完整而恰当地表现题材。

intro.en: Justice adds a Latin-derived noun ending to just; the deeper pieces are jus and justus.
intro.cn: justice 给 just 加了一个拉丁来源的名词词尾，更深的部件是 jus 与 justus。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all descend from jus, law.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都源自 jus「法」。

items.example: A just ruler weighs both sides.
items.exampleCN: 公正的统治者会称量两边。

definition_zh: 射击；发射；拍摄；投篮；嫩芽
definition_en: to fire a weapon, send something out quickly, film something, score in basketball, or a new plant growth
core_image: 镜头对准一只起飞的鸟，快门声在安静的林间响起
scene: 摄影师拍下了鸟起飞的一刻。 The photographer shot the bird taking off.
sceneCN: 这里 shoot 是「拍摄」（第 3 个义项）；句意：摄影师拍下了鸟起飞的一刻。

senses.title: Fire a weapon
senses.definition: to fire a gun or other weapon
senses.definitionCN: 用枪或其他武器开火
senses.example: The guard was told not to shoot.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫被告知不要开枪。
senses.why: This is the basic violent sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的暴力义项。

senses.title: Send out quickly
senses.definition: to send something out with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物送出
senses.example: The rocket shot into the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭射向天空。
senses.why: The firing image extends to fast movement.
senses.whyCN: 开火的意象扩展到快速运动。

senses.title: Film
senses.definition: to record a film or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 录制电影或拍照
senses.example: The photographer shot the bird taking off.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师拍下了鸟起飞的一刻。
senses.why: A camera fires like a gun.
senses.whyCN: 相机像枪一样「开火」。

senses.title: Score a basket
senses.definition: to throw a ball at a goal
senses.definitionCN: 把球投向球篮
senses.example: She shot from the corner and scored.
senses.exampleCN: 她从角落投篮得分。
senses.why: The ball is sent out like a shot.
senses.whyCN: 球像子弹一样被送出。

senses.title: New growth
senses.definition: a young stem or leaf growing from a plant
senses.definitionCN: 植物长出的幼茎或幼叶
senses.example: Green shoots appeared after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后冒出了绿色嫩芽。
senses.why: The plant shoots upward.
senses.whyCN: 植物向上「射」出新芽。

intro.en: Shoot comes from an Old English word meaning to send out swiftly.
intro.cn: shoot 来自古英语中表示快速射出的词。

items.en: Sceotan meant to shoot or throw.
items.cn: sceotan 意为射击或投掷。

items.en: Skeutanan carried the same sense.
items.cn: skeutanan 带有同样的含义。

items.en: Shoot covered arrows, darts, and pain.
items.cn: shoot 涵盖射箭、飞镖与刺痛。

items.en: Shoot extended to cameras and basketball.
items.cn: shoot 扩展到相机与篮球。

items.en: Shoot named new plant growth.
items.cn: shoot 指植物的新芽。

note.en: Shoot is compared with similar-looking words and with words for firing and filming.
note.cn: 把 shoot 与形近词以及表示射击和拍摄的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place where goods are sold
a single firing or photograph
to speak very loudly
to shoot a weapon
to record moving pictures
a young plant growth

normalIntro.en: Shoot is one fast outward movement: a bullet, a ball, a photo, or a new leaf.
normalIntro.cn: shoot 是一次快速向外的运动：子弹、球、照片或新叶。

normal.en: Do not shoot at birds.
normal.cn: 不要向鸟射击。

normal.en: The rocket shot upward.
normal.cn: 火箭向上射去。

normal.en: They are shooting a film here.
normal.cn: 他们在这里拍电影。

normal.en: He shoots hoops after school.
normal.cn: 他放学后投篮。

normal.en: Bamboo shoots are used in soup.
normal.cn: 竹笋被用来做汤。

abstract.en: A camera and a gun both say shoot.
abstract.cn: 相机与枪都说 shoot。

abstract.en: Growth shoots upward without asking.
abstract.cn: 生长不问许可就向上冒。

abstract.en: The fastest things leave no time to think.
abstract.cn: 最快的东西不给人思考的时间。

examples.en: Green shoots appeared after the rain.

dict_mnemonic.text: shoot 的核心是「快速送出」：射出子弹、投出球、按下快门、冒出嫩芽，都是向外射。

root: 源自古英语 sceotan（射击、投掷），核心义「快速向外送出」。

sensesIntro.en: Shoot means to fire, send out, film, throw a ball, or a new plant growth.
sensesIntro.cn: shoot 意为射击、发射、拍摄、投篮或嫩芽。

core.en: Something sent outward fast.
core.cn: 快速向外送出的东西。

branches.en: A weapon fires at a target.
branches.cn: 武器向目标开火。

branches.en: A rocket leaves the ground.
branches.cn: 火箭离开地面。

branches.en: A camera captures a moment.
branches.cn: 相机捕捉一个瞬间。

branches.en: A ball flies toward the hoop.
branches.cn: 球飞向篮筐。

branches.en: A plant pushes out new growth.
branches.cn: 植物推出新芽。

intro.en: Shoot forms a family of firing, filming, and growth words.
intro.cn: shoot 形成一个表示射击、拍摄与生长的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shoot has no Latin ancestor; Latin iacere, to throw, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shoot 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 iacere（投掷）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: the act of firing or filming
a fight with guns or a penalty contest
items.example: The match ended in a shootout.

items.meaning: a fast violent film or game

definition_en: a person who is not named or known, or an important person
core_image: 门口站着一个看不清面孔的人影
scene: 有人在门口等你。 Someone is waiting for you at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 someone 是「某人；有人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：有人在门口等你。

senses.title: An unnamed person
senses.definition: a person who is not named or not known
senses.definitionCN: 没有被指名或不认识的人
senses.example: Someone is waiting for you at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在门口等你。
senses.why: Some plus one names a single person without a name.
senses.whyCN: some 加 one，指一个没有名字的人。

senses.title: An important person
senses.definition: a person of importance or fame
senses.definitionCN: 有地位或名气的人
senses.example: He is someone in the music world.
senses.exampleCN: 他在音乐界是个重要人物。
senses.why: A person can become someone who matters.
senses.whyCN: 一个普通人可以变成举足轻重的人。

intro.en: Someone joins some with the word one.
intro.cn: someone 把 some 与 one 组合在一起。

items.en: Sum meant some; an meant one.
items.cn: sum 意为一些，an 意为一。

items.en: The compound named a single unknown person.
items.cn: 这个复合词指单个不认识的人。

items.en: Someone grew common alongside somebody.
items.cn: someone 与 somebody 一起变得常见。

items.en: It also came to name a person of importance.
items.cn: 它也开始指重要人物。

items.en: It is slightly more formal than somebody in many uses.
items.cn: 在许多用法中它比 somebody 略正式。

note.en: Someone is compared with look-alike words and words for unknown people.
note.cn: 把 someone 与形近词以及表示未知人物的词作比较。

sensesIntro.cn: someone 意为未指名或不认识的人，或重要人物。

core.en: One person, name left open.
